questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle walks 10 m due east and then returns to the starting point along the same line, taking 4 s in all. Its average velocity is:
questions.e: Average velocity is total displacement over total time; the particle returns to its start, so displacement is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A velocity–time graph is a symmetric triangle with peak 20 m/s and total base 10 s. The displacement is:
questions.e: Displacement is the area under the v–t graph: (1/2) × 10 × 20 = 100 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two trains move towards each other at 40 m/s and 60 m/s. The speed of one as seen from the other is:
questions.e: For motion in opposite directions the relative speed is the sum: 40 + 60 = 100 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle's velocity is v = 3t² − 2t (SI units). Its acceleration at t = 2 s is:
questions.e: Acceleration is dv/dt = 6t − 2; at t = 2 s this is 12 − 2 = 10 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle's position is x = 4t³ − 6t (SI units). Its velocity at t = 1 s is:
questions.e: Velocity is dx/dt = 12t² − 6; at t = 1 s this is 12 − 6 = 6 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body falls freely from rest (g = 10 m/s²). The distance it covers during the 3rd second of fall is:
questions.e: Distance in the nth second is (g/2)(2n − 1); for n = 3 this is 5 × 5 = 25 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car brakes to rest with constant deceleration. If its initial speed is doubled, the stopping distance becomes:
questions.e: From v² = 2as, the stopping distance is proportional to v², so doubling v quadruples the distance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two stones are dropped from the same height 1 s apart. When the first has been falling for 3 s (g = 10 m/s²), their separation is:
questions.e: Positions: (1/2)g(3²) and (1/2)g(2²); the separation is 5 × (9 − 4) = 25 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Vectors a and b have magnitudes 3 and 4 units with 30° between them. The magnitude of a × b is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A unit vector in the direction of 6i − 8j is:
questions.e: The magnitude of 6i − 8j is 10, so the unit vector is (6i − 8j)/10 = 0.6i − 0.8j.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a = 2i − j and b = 3i + 4j, the dot product a · b equals:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The scalar triple product [a b c] = a · (b × c) represents, geometrically:
o: The area of the triangle formed by vectors a, b and c
The volume of the parallelepiped formed by vectors a, b and c
The surface area of the parallelepiped formed by vectors a, b and c
The length of the diagonal of the parallelepiped formed by a, b and c
questions.e: a · (b × c) equals the volume of the parallelepiped with coterminous edges a, b and c; it vanishes when the three vectors are coplanar.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two equal forces F act at 60° to each other. The magnitude of their resultant is:
questions.e: Resultant² = F² + F² + 2F²cos 60° = 3F², so the resultant is F√3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A vector makes angles α, β and γ with the positive x, y and z axes respectively. The value of cos²α + cos²β + cos²γ is:
questions.e: The direction cosines of a vector r are cos α = r_x/|r|, cos β = r_y/|r|, cos γ = r_z/|r|; squaring and adding gives (r_x² + r_y² + r_z²)/|r|² = 1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If l, m, n are the direction cosines of a line, then l² + m² + n² equals:
questions.e: Direction cosines are the components of a unit vector, so their squares sum to 1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two vectors of magnitudes 6 and 8 units have 60° between them. The magnitude of their difference is about:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the scalar triple product [a b c] = 0, the three vectors are:
questions.e: A zero scalar triple product means zero volume of the parallelepiped, so the vectors lie in one plane.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity at a depth of R/2 below Earth's surface (R = Earth's radius) is:
questions.e: Inside Earth, g varies linearly with distance from the centre: g′ = g(1 − d/R) = g(1 − 1/2) = g/2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A planet has twice the radius and twice the density of Earth. The escape velocity from its surface is (Earth's escape velocity = 11.2 km/s):
questions.e: v_e = √(2GM/R) with M = (4/3)πR³ρ gives v_e proportional to R√ρ. Doubling both R and ρ multiplies v_e by 2√2 ≈ 2.83, so v_e ≈ 11.2 × 2.83 = 31.7 km/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a satellite at a given height, the ratio of escape velocity to orbital velocity is:
questions.e: Escape velocity is √(2GM/r) and orbital velocity is √(GM/r), so their ratio is √2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A planet orbits its star at twice Earth's orbital radius (same star). Its year is about:
questions.e: By Kepler's third law T² ∝ r³, so doubling r multiplies T by 2√2 ≈ 2.83.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 60 kg astronaut on the Moon (g_moon ≈ 1.67 m/s²) weighs about:
questions.e: Weight = mg = 60 × 1.67 ≈ 100 N, roughly one-sixth of the Earth weight.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The gravitational potential energy of a satellite of mass m at height R/2 above Earth (R = Earth's radius) is:
questions.e: U = −GMm/r with r = R + R/2 = 3R/2, giving U = −GMm/(3R/2) = −(2/3)GMm/R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity is maximum at the:
questions.e: Earth's rotation reduces apparent gravity most at the equator, and the polar radius is smallest, so g peaks at the poles.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If Earth suddenly stopped rotating, the apparent weight of an object at the equator would:
questions.e: Rotation currently subtracts a centrifugal term mω²R from apparent weight; stopping rotation removes it, so apparent weight rises.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Satellite A orbits at radius r and satellite B at radius 4r around the same planet. The ratio of their orbital speeds vA/vB is:
questions.e: Orbital speed is √(GM/r), so vA/vB = √(4r/r) = 2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wheel rotates at 300 revolutions per minute. Its angular velocity is:
questions.e: ω = 2π × (revolutions per second) = 2π × 5 = 10π rad/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle completes 120 revolutions in one minute. Its time period is:
questions.e: 120 revolutions in 60 s means 2 per second, so one revolution takes 0.5 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle moves in a circle of radius 0.5 m with angular speed 4 rad/s. Its centripetal acceleration is:
questions.e: Centripetal acceleration = ω²r = 16 × 0.5 = 8 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A frictionless banked curve of radius 100 m is designed for 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). The banking angle satisfies:
questions.e: For a banked turn tan θ = v²/(rg) = 400/1000 = 0.4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The minimum speed at the top of a vertical circular loop of radius R needed to stay on the track is:
questions.e: At the top, mg alone must supply the centripetal force: mg = mv²/R, giving v = √(gR).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle completes a vertical circle. The tension at the bottom exceeds the tension at the top by:
questions.e: With the minimum speed to complete the circle, v_top² = gR gives T_top = 0; energy conservation gives v_bottom² = 5gR so T_bottom = 6mg, and the difference is 6mg.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A conical pendulum has string length 1 m at 60° to the vertical (g = 10 m/s²). Its time period is about:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle's speed is halved and its orbital radius is doubled. Its centripetal acceleration becomes:
questions.e: a = v²/r; the new value is (v/2)²/(2r) = v²/(8r) = a/8.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A coin rests on a rotating turntable. In the rotating frame, the coin experiences:
o: A force mω²r toward the centre
A force mω²r away from the centre
questions.e: In the rotating frame a centrifugal pseudo-force mω²r acts radially outward on the coin.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A projectile is launched at 30° with speed 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). Its horizontal range is about:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A projectile is launched at 30° with speed 50 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). Its time of flight is:
questions.e: Time of flight = 2u sin θ/g = 2 × 50 × 0.5/10 = 5 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A projectile launched at 45° with speed 20√2 m/s follows y = x − x²/80 (g = 10 m/s²). The point (40 m, 20 m) is:
questions.e: Substituting x = 40 gives y = 40 − 1600/80 = 20, exactly the point's height, so it lies on the trajectory.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A projectile is launched at 60° with speed 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). Its speed at half the maximum height is about:
questions.e: Horizontal speed stays 10 m/s; at half the 15 m max height, vertical speed² = 300 − 150 = 150, so v = √(100 + 150) ≈ 15.8 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball is thrown horizontally at 30 m/s from a 45 m high cliff (g = 10 m/s²). It lands at a horizontal distance of:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A projectile is launched at 30° with speed 30 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). Its maximum height is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two projectiles are launched with the same speed at 30° and 60°. The ratio of their maximum heights is:
questions.e: Max height scales as sin²θ, so the ratio is sin²30°/sin²60° = 0.25/0.75 = 1/3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A projectile is launched at 60° with speed 40 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). Its speed at the highest point is:
questions.e: At the top the vertical component vanishes, leaving only u cos θ = 40 × 0.5 = 20 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two projectiles A (30°) and B (60°) are launched with equal speeds. The ratio of their times of flight TA/TB is:
questions.e: Time of flight scales as sin θ, so TA/TB = sin 30°/sin 60° = 0.5/0.866 = 1/√3.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: For the differential equation (d²y/dx²)² = 1 + (dy/dx)², the order and degree are:
questions.e: The highest derivative is d²y/dx² (order 2) and it appears squared (degree 2).

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The differential equation of the family of curves y = Aeˣ + Be⁻ˣ is:
questions.e: Differentiating twice returns the same exponentials: y′ = Aeˣ − Be⁻ˣ and y″ = Aeˣ + Be⁻ˣ = y.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The solution of dy/dx = (x + 1)/y is:
questions.e: Separating gives y dy = (x + 1)dx, integrating to y²/2 = x²/2 + x + C₁, i.e. y² = x² + 2x + C.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The general solution of dy/dx = y/x is:
questions.e: dy/y = dx/x integrates to ln|y| = ln|x| + C₁, giving y = Cx.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The solution of dy/dx = (x + y)/x is:
questions.e: This is homogeneous; setting y = vx gives x dv/dx = 1, so v = ln|x| + C and y = x ln|x| + Cx.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The general solution of dy/dx + y = eˣ is:
questions.e: The integrating factor is eˣ, giving y·eˣ = ∫e²ˣdx = e²ˣ/2 + C, so y = eˣ/2 + Ce⁻ˣ.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The solution of dy/dx + y tan x = sec x is:
o: y = cos x + C sin x
y = sin x + C cos x
questions.e: The integrating factor is sec x; then y sec x = ∫sec²x dx = tan x + C, giving y = sin x + C cos x.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The particular solution of dy/dx = 3x² with y(1) = 2 is:
questions.e: Integrating gives y = x³ + C; the condition y(1) = 2 fixes C = 1.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The solution of dy/dx = eˣ⁺ʸ is:
questions.e: Separating: e⁻ʸdy = eˣdx; integrating gives −e⁻ʸ = eˣ + C₁, i.e. eˣ + e⁻ʸ = C.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: For x(dy/dx)³ + y = d²y/dx², the order and degree are:
questions.e: The highest derivative is d²y/dx² appearing to the first power: order 2, degree 1.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The orthogonal trajectories of the family y = kx² are:
questions.e: From y = kx², dy/dx = 2y/x; orthogonal trajectories satisfy dy/dx = −x/(2y), giving x² + 2y² = C.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: A bacterial culture satisfies dN/dt = 0.02N. Its doubling time is about:
questions.e: N = N₀e^{0.02t}; doubling needs e^{0.02t} = 2, so t = ln 2/0.02 ≈ 34.7 yr.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The particular solution of dy/dx = sin x cos x with y(0) = 1 is:
questions.e: ∫sin x cos x dx = (sin²x)/2; the condition y(0) = 1 gives the constant 1.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The y-intercept of the line 3x − 4y = 12 is:
questions.e: Setting x = 0 gives −4y = 12, so y = −3.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The slope of the line joining (2, 5) and (6, 13) is:

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The equation of the line through (1, 2) with slope 3 is:
questions.e: Using y − 2 = 3(x − 1) gives y = 3x − 1.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The line through (1, 1) parallel to 2x + 3y = 6 is:
questions.e: A parallel line has the form 2x + 3y = c; through (1,1), c = 5.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The line through the origin perpendicular to 3x − 4y = 7 is:
questions.e: The given slope is 3/4, so the perpendicular slope is −4/3; through the origin this is 4x + 3y = 0.

questions.q: The distance of the point (1, 2) from the line 3x + 4y = 10 is:

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The distance between the parallel lines 3x + 4y = 5 and 3x + 4y = 15 is:

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The acute angle between lines of slopes 1 and −1 is:

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The x- and y-intercepts of x + y = 1 are respectively:
questions.e: Setting y = 0 gives x = 1 and setting x = 0 gives y = 1.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The foot of the perpendicular from the origin to the line x + y = 2 is:
questions.e: By symmetry the closest point on x + y = 2 to the origin is (1, 1).

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The reflection of the point (2, 3) in the y-axis is:
questions.e: Reflection in the y-axis negates the x-coordinate: (−2, 3).

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The centroid of the triangle with vertices (1, 2), (7, 2) and (1, 8) is:
questions.e: The centroid is the average of the vertices: ((1+7+1)/3, (2+2+8)/3) = (3, 4).

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The slope of the tangent to y = x² at x = 2 is:
questions.e: dy/dx = 2x; at x = 2 the slope is 4.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The equation of the tangent to y = x³ at (1, 1) is:
questions.e: Slope = 3x² = 3 at (1,1); the tangent is y − 1 = 3(x − 1), i.e. y = 3x − 2.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The equation of the normal to y = x² at (1, 1) is:
questions.e: The tangent slope is 2, so the normal slope is −1/2; through (1,1): y − 1 = −(x − 1)/2, i.e. x + 2y = 3.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: For f(x) = x⁴ − 4x³, the local minimum occurs at x =
questions.e: f′ = 4x³ − 12x² = 4x²(x − 3); f″ = 12x² − 24x is positive at x = 3, confirming a minimum there.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The maximum value of sin x + cos x is:
questions.e: sin x + cos x = √2 sin(x + π/4), whose maximum is √2.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The function f(x) = eˣ + x is:
questions.e: f′(x) = eˣ + 1 > 0 for all x, so the function increases everywhere.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Two positive numbers sum to 12. Their maximum possible product is:
questions.e: For fixed sum the product is maximised when the numbers are equal: 6 × 6 = 36.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The side of a square increases at 3 cm/s. When the side is 5 cm, its area increases at:
questions.e: A = s² gives dA/dt = 2s·ds/dt = 2 × 5 × 3 = 30 cm²/s.

questions.q: The number of ways to choose 4 people from 12 is:

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The number of distinct words that can be formed from the letters of APPLE is:
questions.e: 5 letters with P repeated twice: 5!/2! = 60.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The number of distinct arrangements of the letters of MISSISSIPPI is:
questions.e: 11 letters with repeats 4, 4, 2: 11!/(4!4!2!) = 34650.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: A team needs 2 men from 5 and 3 women from 4. The number of possible teams is:

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The number of ways to seat 6 people around a round table is:
questions.e: Circular arrangements of n distinct people: (6 − 1)! = 120.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: From 5 distinct objects, the number of non-empty selections is:
questions.e: Every object is either in or out (2⁵ ways) minus the empty selection: 32 − 1 = 31.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The number of 3-letter codes (no repetition) from 7 distinct letters is:

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The number of 3-digit numbers with distinct digits chosen from 1–6 is:
questions.e: 6 choices for the first digit, 5 for the second, 4 for the third: 6 × 5 × 4 = 120.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The number of ways to distribute 4 identical balls into 3 distinct boxes is:

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: From 7 people, the number of 2-member subcommittees is:

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The number of shortest paths along grid lines from (0,0) to (3,3) moving only right or up is:
questions.e: Choose the positions of the 3 right moves among 6 total moves: C(6, 3) = 20.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The number of one-one functions from a 3-element set to a 5-element set is:
questions.e: Choose distinct images in order: P(5, 3) = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The number of onto functions from a 4-element set to a 3-element set is:
questions.e: Inclusion–exclusion: 3⁴ − 3·2⁴ + 3·1⁴ = 81 − 48 + 3 = 36.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: If n(A) = 20, n(B) = 30 and n(A ∩ B) = 12, then n(A ∪ B) equals:

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The number of bijections from a 5-element set to itself is:
questions.e: A bijection is a permutation: 5! = 120.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The function f: R → R, f(x) = x², is:
questions.e: f(−1) = f(1) so it is not one-one, and negative values have no pre-image so it is not onto.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: If f(x) = 2x and g(x) = x + 1, then (f ∘ g)(x) equals:

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The inverse of f(x) = 3x − 2 is:
questions.e: Set y = 3x − 2 and solve for x: x = (y + 2)/3, so f⁻¹(x) = (x + 2)/3.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The number of symmetric relations on a 4-element set is:
questions.e: Symmetric relations are determined by the 4 diagonal and C(4,2) off-diagonal pairs: 2^{4+6} = 1024.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The number of equivalence relations on the set {1, 2, 3} is:
questions.e: Equivalence relations correspond to set partitions; {1,2,3} has 5 partitions (Bell number B₃).

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: The range of f(x) = |x − 1| for x in [0, 2] is:
questions.e: |x − 1| is 0 at x = 1 and rises to 1 at both endpoints, so the range is [0, 1].

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: By De Morgan's law, the complement of A ∪ B is:
questions.e: De Morgan's law: (A ∪ B)′ = A′ ∩ B′.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of ionic radii is:
questions.e: These ions are isoelectronic; the one with the fewest protons (Na⁺) is largest: Na⁺ > Mg²⁺ > Al³⁺.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among Li, Be, B and C, the element with the highest first ionisation energy is:
questions.e: First ionisation energy rises across the period with effective nuclear charge, so C is highest of the four.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of electronegativity is:
questions.e: Electronegativity increases across a period: C < N < O < F, with fluorine the most electronegative element.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among Na, K, Rb and Cs, the most metallic element is:
questions.e: Metallic character increases down a group as the outer electron is lost more easily; Cs is the most metallic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following oxides is amphoteric?
questions.e: Al₂O₃ reacts with both acids and bases, which is the definition of amphoteric.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The diagonal relationship in the periodic table exists between:
questions.e: Li and Mg show similar properties (diagonal relationship), as do Be and Al.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of oxidising power of the halogens is:
questions.e: Oxidising strength falls down the group as electron affinity and electrode potential decrease.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which noble gas readily forms fluorides such as XeF₂ and XeF₄?
questions.e: Xenon's large size and low ionisation energy let it form XeF₂, XeF₄, XeF₆ and oxides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The element with the most exothermic first electron affinity among O, N, S, Se is:
questions.e: Sulphur's electron affinity is the most exothermic of these; oxygen's small size causes electron–electron repulsion that reduces its value.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: First ionisation energy is higher for Mg than for Al because:
questions.e: Magnesium's filled 3s² subshell is extra stable, so removing its electron costs more energy than removing Al's lone 3p electron.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of ionic size for N³⁻, O²⁻ and F⁻ is:
questions.e: These are isoelectronic; fewer protons means weaker pull, so N³⁻ (7 protons) is largest.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In period 3, the element with the largest atomic radius is:
questions.e: Atomic radius decreases across a period, so sodium at the start of period 3 is largest.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which element exhibits the +8 oxidation state in its tetroxide?
questions.e: Osmium forms OsO₄ with osmium in the +8 state, the highest oxidation state known.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The lanthanide contraction is caused by:
questions.e: The 4f electrons shield the nuclear charge poorly, so the radius steadily shrinks across the lanthanides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following oxides is strongly acidic?
questions.e: Non-metal oxides like SO₃ form acids in water (H₂SO₄); the others are basic metal oxides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Doubling [A] doubles the reaction rate and doubling [B] quadruples it. The overall order of the reaction is:
questions.e: The rate is first order in A and second order in B, so the overall order is 1 + 2 = 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a first-order reaction, the fraction of reactant remaining after three half-lives is:
questions.e: Each half-life halves the amount: (1/2)³ = 1/8 remains.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A first-order reaction is 75% complete in 40 min. Its half-life is:
questions.e: 75% completion means two half-lives have passed (1 → 1/2 → 1/4), so t½ = 40/2 = 20 min.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A reaction with Ea = 60 kJ/mol is warmed from 300 K to 310 K. By what factor does k increase? (R = 8.314 J/mol·K)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a mechanism whose slow step is A + B → C, the rate law is:
questions.e: The rate-determining step is the slow one, and its molecularity gives the rate law: r = k[A][B].

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The molecularity of the elementary step 2A → products is:
questions.e: Molecularity counts the reacting species in the elementary step: two molecules of A, so it is bimolecular (2).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A zero-order reaction has [A]₀ = 0.8 M and k = 0.02 M/min. Its half-life is:
questions.e: For zero order t½ = [A]₀/(2k) = 0.8/0.04 = 20 min.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A second-order reaction (single reactant) has k = 0.5 L/mol·min and [A]₀ = 0.2 M. Its half-life is:
questions.e: For second order t½ = 1/(k[A]₀) = 1/(0.5 × 0.2) = 10 min.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A catalyst increases the reaction rate by:
o: Providing an alternative path of lower activation energy
questions.e: A catalyst opens a lower-Ea pathway; it changes neither ΔH nor the equilibrium constant.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the reaction 2A → B, the rate of disappearance of A and the rate of appearance of B are related by:
questions.e: The unique reaction rate is −(1/2)d[A]/dt = d[B]/dt, dividing by stoichiometric coefficients.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The concentration of A falls from 0.60 M to 0.20 M in 10 min. The average rate of disappearance of A is:
questions.e: Average rate = −Δ[A]/Δt = 0.40/10 = 0.04 M/min.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: A copper wire of cross-section 1 mm² carries 2 A. With free-electron density 8.5×10²⁸ m⁻³, the drift velocity is about:
questions.e: v_d = I/(neA) = 2/(8.5×10²⁸ × 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ × 10⁻⁶) ≈ 1.47×10⁻⁴ m/s. Electrons drift at a crawl — the electric signal travels near light speed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge, P = 2 Ω, Q = 4 Ω and R = 6 Ω. The unknown resistance S is:
questions.e: Balance condition P/Q = R/S → S = Q×R/P = 4×6/2 = 12 Ω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A potentiometer balances the EMF of two cells at 75 cm and 50 cm of wire. The ratio of the EMFs E₁/E₂ is:
questions.e: At null point E ∝ balancing length, so E₁/E₂ = l₁/l₂ = 75/50 = 3/2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A bulb rated 60 W, 220 V is operated at 110 V. The power it actually dissipates is about:
questions.e: Filament resistance R = V²/P = 220²/60 ≈ 807 Ω. At 110 V: P = V²/R = 12100/807 ≈ 15 W — quarter the voltage gives quarter the power.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. The image is formed at:
o: 30 cm in front, same size, inverted
15 cm in front, half size, erect
questions.e: Cartesian: u = −30, f = −15. 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/15 + 1/30 = −1/30 → v = −30 cm (real, in front). m = −v/u = −(−30)/(−30) = −1: same size, inverted. Object at C gives image at C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The critical angle for glass of refractive index 1.5 is about:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A biconvex lens (μ = 1.5) has radii of curvature 30 cm each. Its focal length is:
questions.e: 1/f = (1.5 − 1)(1/30 − 1/(−30)) = 0.5 × (2/30) = 1/30 → f = 30 cm. (R₂ is negative for biconvex in Cartesian convention.)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A coin at the bottom of a 12 cm deep vessel of water (μ = 4/3) appears to be at a depth of:
questions.e: Apparent depth = real depth / μ = 12/(4/3) = 9 cm — objects in water look raised.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 20 cm. The combination acts as:
questions.e: 1/F = 1/20 + 1/(−20) = 0, so F = ∞ and P = 5 + (−5) = 0 dioptre — the powers cancel exactly.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of atoms present in 8 g of O₂ is:
questions.e: 8 g O₂ = 8/32 = 0.25 mol of O₂ molecules. Atoms = 0.25 × 2 × N_A = 0.5 × 6.022×10²³ = 3.011×10²³. Remember each O₂ has 2 atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A compound contains 40% C, 6.67% H and 53.33% O by mass. Its empirical formula is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 10 g H₂ and 64 g O₂ react as 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. The mass of water formed is:
questions.e: n(H₂) = 10/2 = 5 mol, n(O₂) = 64/32 = 2 mol. Ratios: 5/2 = 2.5, 2/1 = 2 — O₂ is limiting. H₂O formed = 2 × 2 = 4 mol = 4 × 18 = 72 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 4 g of NaOH dissolved in water to make 250 mL of solution. The molarity is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 18 g of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) is dissolved in 90 g of water. The mole fraction of glucose is about:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A first-order reaction has k = 0.0231 min⁻¹. Its half-life is:
questions.e: t½ = 0.693/k = 0.693/0.0231 = 30 min. For first order the half-life is independent of initial concentration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The units of the rate constant for a third-order reaction are:
questions.e: Units of k = mol^(1−n)·L^(n−1)·s⁻¹. For n = 3: mol⁻²·L²·s⁻¹ = L²·mol⁻²·s⁻¹.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For rate = k[A][B]², doubling [A] and doubling [B] changes the rate by a factor of:
questions.e: Rate ∝ [A]¹[B]². New rate = k(2[A])(2[B])² = 2 × 4 = 8 times the original.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A reaction with Ea = 50 kJ/mol is warmed from 300 K to 310 K. By what factor does k increase? (R = 8.314 J/mol·K)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A zero-order reaction proceeds at 0.05 M/min starting from 1.0 M. The time to reach 0.25 M is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Formaldehyde (HCHO) with concentrated KOH undergoes Cannizzaro reaction to give:
questions.e: HCHO has no α-hydrogen, so with conc. KOH one molecule is oxidised to formate (HCOOK) and another reduced to methanol (CH₃OH) — disproportionation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: CH₃CONH₂ on treatment with Br₂ and KOH gives:
questions.e: Hoffmann bromamide degradation: RCONH₂ + Br₂/KOH → RNH₂ with one carbon fewer. CH₃CONH₂ → CH₃NH₂ (methylamine).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Phenol with CHCl₃ and aqueous NaOH at 340 K gives mainly:
questions.e: Reimer–Tiemann reaction: phenol + CHCl₃/NaOH introduces a −CHO group ortho to −OH, giving salicylaldehyde as the major product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 2CH₃CH₂Br + 2Na (dry ether) → ? This is an example of:
questions.e: Wurtz reaction: 2R−X + 2Na → R−R + 2NaX. Two ethyl bromides couple to n-butane (CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Benzene diazonium chloride with CuCl/HCl gives:
questions.e: Sandmeyer reaction: ArN₂⁺Cl⁻ + CuCl/HCl → ArCl + N₂. The diazo group is replaced by chlorine, giving chlorobenzene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The spin-only magnetic moment of Mn²⁺ (3d⁵) is:
questions.e: Mn²⁺ is d⁵ with n = 5 unpaired electrons. μ = √[n(n+2)] = √35 ≈ 5.92 BM.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of these aqueous ions is colourless?
questions.e: Colour needs d–d transitions, i.e. partially filled d-orbitals. Zn²⁺ is d¹⁰ (full) — no d–d transition possible, so colourless. Cu²⁺ (blue), Fe²⁺ (green), Ni²⁺ (green) are coloured.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The highest oxidation state shown by manganese is:
questions.e: Mn shows +2 to +7; the maximum +7 appears in Mn₂O₇ and the permanganate ion MnO₄⁻, using all 7 valence electrons (3d⁵4s²).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The equivalent weight of KMnO₄ (M = 158) in acidic medium is:
questions.e: In acid, MnO₄⁻ gains 5 electrons (Mn⁺⁷ → Mn⁺²), so n-factor = 5. Eq. wt. = 158/5 = 31.6.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The electronic configuration of chromium (Z = 24) is:
questions.e: Cr adopts [Ar]3d⁵4s¹ because the half-filled d-subshell is extra stable — the classic anomalous configuration.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation 4x² + kx + 9 = 0 has equal roots. The value(s) of k are:
questions.e: Equal roots need D = 0: k² − 4×4×9 = 0 → k² = 144 → k = ±12.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If α and β are the roots of x² − 6x + 5 = 0, then α² + β² equals:
questions.e: α + β = 6, αβ = 5. α² + β² = (α+β)² − 2αβ = 36 − 10 = 26 — no need to find the roots (1 and 5).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: One root of x² + kx + 12 = 0 is 3. Then k and the other root are:
questions.e: Product of roots = 12, so the other root = 12/3 = 4. Sum = −k = 3 + 4 = 7 → k = −7. (Check: 9 − 21 + 12 = 0 ✓.)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The maximum value of −x² + 6x − 5 is:
questions.e: a < 0 so the vertex is a maximum: −D/4a with D = 36 − 20 = 16 → −16/(−4) = 4, at x = −b/2a = 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two dice are thrown. The probability that the sum is 8 is:
questions.e: Favourable pairs: (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2) — 5 outcomes out of 36. So P = 5/36.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Events A and B are independent with P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.4. P(neither A nor B) is:
questions.e: P(neither) = P(A')·P(B') = (1 − 0.3)(1 − 0.4) = 0.7 × 0.6 = 0.42. Independence lets us multiply the complements.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A card is drawn from a well-shuffled deck. The probability that it is a king or a queen is:
questions.e: 4 kings + 4 queens = 8 favourable out of 52. P = 8/52 = 2/13. The events are mutually exclusive, so just add.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Bag I has 3 red and 2 white balls; Bag II has 2 red and 3 white. A bag is chosen at random and a red ball is drawn. The probability it came from Bag I is:

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Three fair coins are tossed. The probability of getting at least two heads is:
questions.e: Favourable: exactly 2 heads (³C₂ = 3 ways) + exactly 3 heads (1 way) = 4 out of 8. P = 4/8 = 1/2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: lim(x→0) (sin 5x)/(2x) equals:
questions.e: (sin 5x)/(2x) = (5/2)·(sin 5x)/(5x). As x→0, (sin 5x)/(5x) → 1, so the limit is 5/2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For f(x) = x³ − 3x² − 9x + 20, the local maximum value is:
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² − 6x − 9 = 3(x − 3)(x + 1). Critical points x = 3, −1. f′ changes + → − at x = −1 (max). f(−1) = −1 − 3 + 9 + 20 = 25. (Local min at x = 3 is −7.)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The function f(x) = |x − 2| at x = 2 is:
questions.e: LHL = RHL = f(2) = 0, so continuous. But LHD = −1 and RHD = +1 — the sharp corner means no unique tangent, so not differentiable.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the tangent to y = x³ at the point (1, 1) is:
questions.e: dy/dx = 3x², so slope at (1,1) is 3. Tangent: y − 1 = 3(x − 1) → y = 3x − 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For a = (1, 2, 2) and b = (2, 1, −2), the angle between them is:
questions.e: a·b = 2 + 2 − 4 = 0. A zero dot product means the vectors are perpendicular, so θ = 90°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If a = (3, 0, 0) and b = (0, 4, 0), then |a × b| equals:
questions.e: a × b = (0, 0, 12), so |a × b| = 12. Geometrically this is the area of the 3×4 rectangle they span.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The projection of vector (2, 3, 4) on the x-axis is:
questions.e: Projection on the x-axis (unit vector î = (1,0,0)) is the dot product (2,3,4)·(1,0,0) = 2 — simply the x-component.

questions.e: a = v²/r = 100/25 = 4 m/s², directed toward the centre of the curve.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: A 5 kg block rests on a surface with μs = 0.4. The maximum static friction is (g = 10 m/s²):
questions.e: f_max = μs·N = 0.4×5×10 = 20 N. Any push below this won't move the block.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: A variable force F = 3x² (newtons, x in metres) acts from x = 0 to x = 2 m. The work done is:
questions.e: W = ∫₀² 3x² dx = [x³]₀² = 8 J.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: In SHM given by x = 4 sin(2πt) (SI units), the maximum speed is:
questions.e: v_max = Aω = 4×2π = 8π m/s.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: A wave is described by y = 0.05 sin(10πt − 2πx) (SI). Its speed is:
questions.e: ω = 10π, k = 2π, so v = ω/k = 10π/2π = 5 m/s.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Light of wavelength 400 nm falls on a metal with work function 2.0 eV. The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons is:
questions.e: Photon energy = 1240/400 = 3.1 eV. KE_max = 3.1 − 2.0 = 1.1 eV (Einstein's equation).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The magnetic flux through a coil is Φ = 5t² − 2t + 3 (SI). The magnitude of induced EMF at t = 1 s is:
questions.e: e = −dΦ/dt = −(10t − 2). At t = 1: e = −8 V, magnitude 8 V.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The number of molecules in 4.4 g of CO₂ is:
questions.e: 4.4 g CO₂ = 4.4/44 = 0.1 mol → 0.1×N_A = 6.022×10²² molecules.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The pH of 0.01 M HCl solution is:
questions.e: HCl is a strong acid: [H⁺] = 0.01 M → pH = −log(10⁻²) = 2.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: For N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), the relation between Kp and Kc is:
questions.e: Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn with Δn = 2 − 4 = −2, so Kp = Kc(RT)⁻².

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The standard EMF of the Daniell cell Zn|Zn²⁺||Cu²⁺|Cu is (E° Zn²⁺/Zn = −0.76 V, Cu²⁺/Cu = +0.34 V):
questions.e: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.34 − (−0.76) = 1.10 V.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: In [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃, the oxidation state of cobalt and its coordination number are:
questions.e: 3Cl⁻ balance [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺; NH₃ is neutral, so Co is +3. Six NH₃ ligands → coordination number 6.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃ is:
questions.e: Longest chain has 5 carbons with a methyl branch on carbon 3 → 3-methylpentane.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The hybridisation of carbon in CH₄ and boron in BF₃ are respectively:
questions.e: CH₄: 4 bond pairs, tetrahedral → sp³. BF₃: 3 bond pairs, trigonal planar → sp².

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The most stable carbocation among CH₃⁺, CH₃CH₂⁺, (CH₃)₂CH⁺, (CH₃)₃C⁺ is:
questions.e: Stability: tertiary > secondary > primary > methyl, due to hyperconjugation and the +I effect of alkyl groups. (CH₃)₃C⁺ has 9 hyperconjugative structures.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Monochlorination of n-butane gives how many structural isomers?
questions.e: n-butane CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ has two types of hydrogen (primary on C1/C4, secondary on C2/C3) → 1-chlorobutane and 2-chlorobutane: 2 isomers.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: In the Lucas test (conc. HCl + ZnCl₂), the fastest turbidity appears with:
questions.e: Lucas reagent reacts via carbocation formation: tertiary alcohols react immediately (turbidity at once), secondary in ~5 min, primary only on heating.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal AgNO₃) gives a silver mirror with:
questions.e: Tollens' oxidises aldehydes (RCHO → RCOO⁻) depositing silver; ketones don't react. Acetaldehyde is the only aldehyde listed.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The correct order of basicity in aqueous solution is:
questions.e: In water, solvation of the conjugate acid dominates: secondary > tertiary > primary > ammonia for ethylamines. (In the gas phase the order would follow the +I effect: tertiary highest.)

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Which of the following is a disaccharide?
questions.e: Sucrose = glucose + fructose (a disaccharide). Glucose and fructose are monosaccharides; starch is a polysaccharide.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The number of distinct arrangements of the letters of the word 'JEE' is:
questions.e: 3 letters with E repeated twice: 3!/2! = 3 (JEE, EJE, EEJ).

questions.e: General term ⁵C_r xʳ; r = 3 → ⁵C₃ = 10.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: d/dx [sin(3x)] equals:
questions.e: Chain rule: derivative of sin(3x) is cos(3x)×3 = 3cos(3x).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The value of ∫₀¹ x² dx is:
questions.e: ∫x² dx = x³/3; evaluated 0→1 gives 1/3.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The value of ∫₀^π sin x dx is:
questions.e: ∫sin x dx = −cos x; [−cos x]₀^π = −(−1) − (−1) = 2.

questions.e: F = ma → [M][LT⁻²] = [MLT⁻²].

questions.e: P = ρgh = 1000×10×10 = 10⁵ Pa — about 1 atmosphere.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The rms speed of gas molecules doubles when the absolute temperature is:
questions.e: v_rms ∝ √T. To double v_rms, T must increase by 2² = 4 times.

questions.e: R_total = 10 Ω → I = 20/10 = 2 A (same through all in series).

questions.e: Cartesian: u = −15, f = +10. 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30 → v = +30 cm (real, inverted, magnified).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: A radioactive sample has half-life 2 hours. The fraction remaining after 6 hours is:
questions.e: 6 hours = 3 half-lives → remaining = (1/2)³ = 1/8.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The most electronegative element is:
questions.e: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity (3.98 on the Pauling scale).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The shape of the ammonia (NH₃) molecule is:
questions.e: 3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair → tetrahedral electron geometry, pyramidal molecular shape (lone pair repels).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: For H₂(g) + ½O₂(g) → H₂O(l), Δn_g equals:
questions.e: Δn_g = moles of gaseous products − reactants = 0 − 1.5 = −1.5 (liquid water doesn't count).

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Lithium shows a diagonal relationship with:
questions.e: Li resembles Mg diagonally (similar polarising power): both form nitrides, Li₂CO₃ and MgCO₃ decompose similarly.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The inert-pair effect makes which oxidation state most stable for lead?
questions.e: The 6s² electrons resist bonding (inert-pair effect), so Pb²⁺ is more stable than Pb⁴⁺ — PbCl₄ is a strong oxidant while PbCl₂ is stable.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The order of reactivity toward SN1 hydrolysis (aqueous) is:
questions.e: SN1 rate follows carbocation stability: tertiary > secondary > primary > methyl.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Among phenol, p-cresol and p-nitrophenol, the most acidic is:
questions.e: The −NO₂ group withdraws electrons (−I, −M), stabilising the phenoxide ion; the +I methyl group in p-cresol destabilises it. Acidity: p-nitrophenol > phenol > p-cresol.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Williamson ether synthesis uses:
questions.e: R−ONa + R′−X → R−O−R′ + NaX — an SN2 attack of alkoxide on the alkyl halide.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: Which of the following does NOT give a positive iodoform test?
questions.e: The test needs CH₃CO− or CH₃CH(OH)−. Methanol (CH₃OH) has no methyl group attached to C=O or CH−OH, so it fails.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: The correct order of acid strength is:
questions.e: −I effect: F > Cl > Br, so electron withdrawal (and acid strength) follows FCH₂COOH > ClCH₂COOH > BrCH₂COOH > CH₃COOH.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: A common antacid ingredient is:
questions.e: Magnesium hydroxide (milk of magnesia) is a weak base that neutralises excess stomach HCl.

questions.e: Standard limit: (eˣ − 1)/x → 1 as x → 0.

questions.e: Polynomials are continuous at every real number.

questions.e: f = 10x − x²; f′ = 10 − 2x = 0 → x = 5. f(5) = 25, and f′′ = −2 < 0 confirms a maximum.

questions.e: ∫2x dx = 2·x²/2 + C = x² + C.

questions.subject: Practice Paper
questions.q: For the differential equation (d²y/dx²)³ + dy/dx = 0, the order and degree are:
questions.e: Highest derivative is d²y/dx² → order 2; its power is 3 → degree 3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Who won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics?
questions.e: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics (announced 6 October 2026) went to Francis Halzen for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which statement about neutrinos is correct?
o: They are easily absorbed by lead
They are neutral, near-massless and interact very weakly
questions.e: Neutrinos are electrically neutral, near-massless particles that interact extremely weakly — they can only be detected when they collide with matter. Halzen’s idea was to turn Antarctic ice into a giant detector (IceCube) for such collisions, revealing high-energy cosmic neutrinos.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The final pair of Redwire Roll-Out Solar Arrays delivered to the ISS by SpaceX CRS-35 (13 Oct 2026) can each provide:
o: More than 20 kW of power for over 10 years
More than 10 kW of power for 5 years
More than 50 kW of power for 20 years
More than 5 kW of power for 3 years
questions.e: Each of the final ROSA pair, built by Redwire Space and delivered aboard CRS-35, can provide more than 20 kW of power for more than 10 years.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.q: NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, releasing 15 October 2026, is best described as:
o: A 74-billion-parameter, 9-billion-active-parameter mixture-of-experts model compressed to 24 GB with 2-bit quantization
A 74-billion-parameter dense model requiring 140 GB VRAM
questions.e: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is a 74B-parameter, 9B-active-parameter MoE model compressed to 24 GB via 2-bit quantization, purpose-built for agentic AI on RTX Spark and fully open source (training data, weights, recipes).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What is the electric charge of a neutrino?
questions.e: Neutrinos are electrically neutral (charge zero) — which is why they interact so weakly with matter and need giant detectors like IceCube.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Asymmetric synthesis is a reaction that:
o: Produces equal amounts of both enantiomers
Produces predominantly one enantiomer of a chiral product
questions.e: Asymmetric synthesis preferentially produces one enantiomer of a chiral molecule — the achievement recognised in the 2026 Chemistry Nobel to Kagan and Soai.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The IceCube Neutrino Observatory is located in:
questions.e: IceCube is a cubic-kilometre array of detectors frozen into the ice at the South Pole, Antarctica.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In autocatalysis, the catalyst is:

questions.e: In autocatalysis, a reaction product catalyses its own formation, so the rate accelerates as product builds up — key to Soai’s Nobel-winning work.

questions.e: The SI unit of electrical resistance is the ohm (Ω), named after Georg Ohm; resistance R = V/I.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A projectile is launched with speed u at angle θ to the horizontal. The time of flight T and the maximum height H satisfy which relation between H, T and g?
questions.e: T = 2u sinθ/g and H = u²sin²θ/(2g). Eliminating u sinθ gives H = gT²/8.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere of mass M and radius R rolls without slipping down an incline. Its moment of inertia about its centre is (2/5)MR². The acceleration of its centre of mass is:
questions.e: For rolling without slipping, a = g sinθ/(1 + k²/R²) with k² = (2/5)R², giving a = (5/7) g sinθ.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of ∫₀π/2 sin²x dx is:
questions.e: Using sin²x = (1 − cos2x)/2: ∫₀π/2 sin²x dx = [x/2 − sin2x/4]₀π/2 = π/4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Two dice are thrown. The probability that the sum of the numbers shown is 9 is:
questions.e: Favourable pairs: (3,6), (4,5), (5,4), (6,3) — 4 outcomes out of 36, so P = 4/36 = 1/9.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The IUPAC name of CH3–CH2–CH(CH3)–CH2–CH3 is:
questions.e: The longest chain has 5 carbons with a methyl substituent on carbon 3: 3-methylpentane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For an ideal gas undergoing a reversible isothermal expansion, which of the following is true?
questions.e: For an ideal gas, internal energy depends only on temperature, so in an isothermal process ΔU = 0; by the first law, w = −q (work done by the system equals heat absorbed).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two resistors R and 3R are connected in parallel across a battery. The ratio of the powers dissipated in R and 3R is:
questions.e: For a parallel combination the voltage across each resistor is the same, so P = V^2/R. P(R)/P(3R) = (V^2/R)/(V^2/3R) = 3, i.e. 3 : 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The element with the highest first ionisation enthalpy among the following is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a satellite in circular orbit of radius r around a planet of mass M, how does orbital speed v vary with r?
questions.e: For a satellite in circular orbit: centripetal force = gravitational pull, mv²/r = GMm/r², so v = √(GM/r) — orbital speed decreases as radius increases (v ∝ 1/√r). MMX must match Phobos's orbital speed around Mars for rendezvous.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What is Earth's escape velocity?
questions.e: Escape velocity vₑ = √(2GM/R) = √2 × v₀, where v₀ = √(GM/R) is the orbital speed just above the surface. For Earth: v₀ ≈ 7.9 km/s, so vₑ ≈ 11.2 km/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 10 N horizontal force pushes a block 5 m on a frictionless surface. What is the change in kinetic energy?
questions.e: Work–energy theorem: W_net = ΔK. With constant force F over displacement d at angle θ: W = Fd cosθ. For the block: W = 10 × 5 × cos0° = 50 J, so ΔK = 50 J.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A first-order reaction has rate constant k = 0.0693 min⁻¹. What is its half-life?
questions.e: For a first-order reaction: t₁/₂ = 0.693/k, independent of initial concentration. k = 0.0693 min⁻¹ → t₁/₂ = 0.693/0.0693 = 10 min.

capsules.subject: Exam Info
capsules.title: JEE Main 2027 Session 1: 22–30 Jan 2027; registration expected late Oct 2026
capsules.body: The National Testing Agency’s tentative calendar places JEE Main 2027 Session 1 on 22, 23, 24, 28, 29 and 30 January 2027 (31 January buffer). The online registration is expected in late October 2026 at jeemain.nta.nic.in (last year it began 31 October 2025), with about a month to apply; the Session 2 window opens in February 2027. Keep ready: live photograph, signature, Class 10 certificate, category/PwD proof. Paper 1 (B.E./B.Tech) has 75 questions for 300 marks with negative marking.

capsules.subject: Physics
capsules.title: Nobel Physics 2026: Francis Halzen, IceCube and cosmic neutrinos (6 Oct)
capsules.body: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics (announced 6 October 2026) went to Belgian-born Francis Halzen for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy cosmic neutrinos. Neutrinos — neutral, near-massless ‘ghost particles’ — are detected only when they collide with matter; Halzen turned vast Antarctic ice into a detector for such collisions. For JEE: recall that neutrinos have no electric charge and extraordinarily small mass, and that IceCube is buried in Antarctic ice.

capsules.subject: Technology
capsules.title: NVIDIA's 13 October 2026 announcements: RTX Spark, Nemotron, PAIR
capsules.body: On 13 October 2026 NVIDIA announced: RTX Spark laptops launch 16 October; Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB releases 15 October (74B params, 9B active MoE, 2-bit quantization, fully open source); and PAIR (Personal AI Router) is out of beta — a free, open-source tool distributing AI workloads across compatible PCs on a local network, with llama.cpp support and direct Hugging Face model downloads.

capsules.subject: Physics
capsules.title: Nobel Physics 2026: Francis Halzen and the IceCube Neutrino Observatory
capsules.body: Francis Halzen (University of Wisconsin–Madison) won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory — a cubic-kilometre detector buried in Antarctic ice — and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.

capsules.subject: Chemistry
capsules.title: Nobel Chemistry 2026: asymmetric organic synthesis
capsules.body: Henri B. Kagan (France) and Kenso Soai (Japan) won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for discovering non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis: reactions that selectively produce one enantiomer of a chiral molecule, a cornerstone of modern pharmaceutical chemistry.

capsules.subject: Physics
capsules.title: Space Zone India demonstrates mid-air rocket engine restart with RRR-1
capsules.body: Chennai-based Space Zone India demonstrated a mid-air rocket engine restart with its RRR-1 vehicle using hybrid propulsion — a foundational capability for reusable launch systems, enabling propulsion-assisted manoeuvres, trajectory corrections and controlled deceleration. The mission, RHUMI TWIN 2026, was led by founder Anand Megalingam.

capsules.subject: Exam Updates
capsules.title: JEE Main 2027 Session 1 registration expected this month
capsules.body: NTA is expected to open JEE Main 2027 Session 1 registration in late October/early November 2026 at jeemain.nta.nic.in (last year it opened 31 October). Session 1 is scheduled for 22, 23, 24, 28, 29 and 30 January 2027 (31 January buffer day); Session 2 is expected in April 2027, and the best of the two sessions counts for the final rank.

capsules.subject: Exam Updates
capsules.title: Army TES-57 needs JEE Main 2026
capsules.body: The Indian Army Technical Entry Scheme TES-57 (notification out 14 October 2026) requires Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics (60%) plus appearance in JEE Main 2026. Applications run 14 October-12 November 2026 at joinindianarmy.nic.in for 90 vacancies; the course commences July 2027 and 4-year training leads to a Permanent Commission as Lieutenant.

capsules.subject: Practice Paper
capsules.title: JEE Main stays on CBT mode as NEET goes digital (Oct 2026)
capsules.body: JEE Main continues to be conducted in computer-based mode for its 11.23 lakh candidates, even as the Centre announces NEET's move to online testing — a contrast highlighted in October 2026 reporting. The NTA conducts JEE Main, CUET-UG/PG, UGC-NET and CSIR UGC-NET as computer-based tests already, and the Ministry of Education is formulating a national examination-grade CBT infrastructure strategy (30 September 2026), with the final call on NEET's shift awaiting the Nandan Nilekani-led task force report.

capsules.subject: Practice Paper
capsules.title: Parliamentary panel: JEE/NEET should test school-curriculum concepts, not coaching tricks (Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The parliamentary standing committee on education (382nd report, chaired by Mukul Wasnik, presented October 2026) recommended that NEET, JEE (Main) and CUET test conceptual understanding based on the official school curriculum rather than coaching-specific techniques, alongside a regulatory framework for coaching institutes covering fee transparency, safety and students' mental health.

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: ISRO robotics week: Genrobotics boom arm, IIIT-Dharwad quadcopter, Muks humanoid (14–16 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: Kerala's Genrobotics won an ISRO (URSC) contract for a high-precision boom arm for satellite assembly. IIIT-Dharwad's seven-member Team Icarus finished fourth in the ISRO Robotics Challenge–URSC 2026 with an autonomous heavy-payload quadcopter navigating a GPS-denied Mars-like environment (visual-inertial + optical-flow navigation, computer-vision target detection). Pune's Muks Robotics secured an ISRO project for SPACEO Prime, India's first humanoid space worker. (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Science & Tech
capsules.title: Gaganyaan: Crew Module–Service Module separation tests completed at VSSC (16 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Formula Handbook
capsules.title: Formula Handbook — Physics: Current Electricity
capsules.body:
Circuit basics
Current i = dq/dt · Drift speed vd = i/(neA) · Mobility μ = vd/E
Resistance R = ρL/A · ρ varies as ρ = ρ₀[1 + α(T − T₀)] · Ohm’s law V = iR
Terminal voltage: V = E − ir (discharging), V = E + ir (charging)

Combinations & laws
Series: R = R₁ + R₂ + … · Parallel: 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + …
Kirchhoff: Σi = 0 at a junction; ΣV = 0 around a loop
Power P = Vi = i²R = V²/R · Heat H = i²Rt

Instruments & bridges
Wheatstone balance: P/Q = R/S · Metre bridge: P/Q = l/(100 − l)
Potentiometer: E₁/E₂ = l₁/l₂ · Internal resistance r = R(l₁ − l₂)/l₂
Ammeter shunt S = G·Ig/(I − Ig) · Voltmeter series resistance = V/Ig − G
RC circuit: q = q₀(1 − e−t/RC); time constant τ = RC

capsules.subject: Formula Handbook
capsules.title: Formula Handbook — Physics: Ray & Wave Optics
capsules.body:
Reflection & refraction
Mirror / lens (Cartesian): 1/v + 1/u = 1/f · m = −v/u (mirror), m = v/u (lens)
Lensmaker: 1/f = (μ − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂) · Lens power P = 100/f (f in cm), in dioptre; combined P = P₁ + P₂
Snell: μ = sin i / sin r = c/v · Apparent depth = real depth / μ · Critical angle: sin C = 1/μ

Prism
δ = i + e − A · Minimum deviation: μ = sin[(A + δm)/2] / sin(A/2) · Thin prism: δ = (μ − 1)A

Wave optics
YDSE fringe width β = λD/d · Bright: d sinθ = nλ; dark: d sinθ = (2n − 1)λ/2
Single-slit minima: a sinθ = nλ · Central maximum width = 2λD/a
Telescope resolving limit: θ = 1.22λ/D · Brewster: tan ip = μ

capsules.subject: Formula Handbook
capsules.title: Formula Handbook — Physics: Modern Physics
capsules.body:
Photoelectric effect
hν = φ₀ + Kmax · eV₀ = hν − φ₀ · Threshold ν₀ = φ₀/h · Photon momentum p = h/λ

Matter waves & Bohr atom
de Broglie: λ = h/(mv) = h/√(2mK) · For an electron accelerated through V volts: λ(Å) ≈ 12.27/√V
Bohr radius rn = 0.53 n²/Z Å · Energy En = −13.6 Z²/n² eV · Speed vn = 2.19 × 10⁶ Z/n m/s
Spectral lines: 1/λ = R(1/n₁² − 1/n₂²), R = 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹

Nuclei & radioactivity
Binding energy = [Z·mp + (A − Z)·mn − M]c² · Q-value = (minitial − mfinal)c²
N = N₀e−λt · Half-life T½ = 0.693/λ · Mean life τ = 1/λ · Activity A = λN
Semiconductor diode: i = Is(eV/ηVT − 1)

capsules.subject: Formula Handbook
capsules.title: Formula Handbook — Physics: Thermodynamics & Kinetic Theory
capsules.body:
First law & processes
ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW (ΔU depends only on initial and final states)
Isothermal work: W = nRT ln(V₂/V₁) · Adiabatic work: W = (P₁V₁ − P₂V₂)/(γ − 1)
Adiabatic relations: PVγ = const · TVγ−1 = const · TγP1−γ = const
Cp − Cv = R · γ = Cp/Cv (monoatomic 5/3, diatomic 7/5)

Engines
Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T₂/T₁ = 1 − Q₂/Q₁ (T in kelvin) · Refrigerator COP = Q₂/(Q₁ − Q₂)

Kinetic theory
Pressure P = (1/3)ρc²̄ · vrms = √(3RT/M) = √(3P/ρ) · vavg = √(8RT/πM) · vmp = √(2RT/M)
Internal energy U = (f/2)nRT (f = degrees of freedom) · Mean free path λ = 1/(√2 π d²n)

capsules.subject: Formula Handbook
capsules.title: Formula Handbook — Physics: Rotational Motion & Gravitation
capsules.body:
Moments of inertia
Ring MR² · Disc ½MR² · Solid sphere (2/5)MR² · Hollow sphere (2/3)MR² · Rod about centre ML²/12, about end ML²/3 · Solid cylinder ½MR²
Parallel axis: I = ICM + Md² · Perpendicular axis (planar): Iz = Ix + Iy

Dynamics
τ = Iα = dL/dt · L = Iω = r × p · KE = ½Iω²
Pure rolling (v = ωR): KE = ½Mv²(1 + K²/R²), K = radius of gyration

Gravitation
F = Gm₁m₂/r² · g = GM/R² · Height (small h): gh ≈ g(1 − 2h/R) · Depth: gd = g(1 − d/R)
Escape speed ve = √(2gR) = 11.2 km/s · Orbital speed vo = √(GM/r)
Satellite: KE = +GMm/2r, PE = −GMm/r, Total E = −GMm/2r · Kepler: T² ∝ r³

capsules.subject: Formula Handbook
capsules.title: Formula Handbook — Chemistry: Chemical Bonding & Structure
capsules.body:
Bond parameters
Dipole moment μ = q × d · % ionic character = (μobserved/μ100% ionic) × 100
Bond order (MOT) = (Nb − Na)/2 — O₂: 2 (paramagnetic), O₂⁺: 2.5, O₂⁻: 1.5, O₂²⁻: 1

VSEPR quick table (electron pairs → shape, angle)
2 → Linear, 180° · 3 → Trigonal planar, 120° · 4 → Tetrahedral, 109.5° · 5 → Trigonal bipyramidal, 120°/90° · 6 → Octahedral, 90°
With lone pairs: NH₃ — sp³, pyramidal (107°) · H₂O — sp³, bent (104.5°) · SF₄ — sp³d, see-saw · ClF₃ — sp³d, T-shaped · XeF₄ — sp³d², square planar · XeF₂ — sp³d, linear

Key trends
Hybridisation = count σ-bonds + lone pairs on the central atom
Fajans’ rules: small cation + large anion + high charge ⇒ covalent character increases
H-bond strength: HF > H₂O > NH₃; intramolecular H-bonding (o-nitrophenol) lowers boiling point
Lattice energy ∝ (q₁q₂)/r₀ — higher charge, smaller ions ⇒ stronger lattice

capsules.subject: Formula Handbook
capsules.title: Formula Handbook — Chemistry: Coordination Compounds
capsules.body:
Basics
EAN = Z − (oxidation number) + 2 × (coordination number)
Spectrochemical series (weak → strong field): I⁻ < Br⁻ < S²⁻ < SCN⁻ < Cl⁻ < F⁻ < OH⁻ < C₂O₄²⁻ < H₂O < NCS⁻ < NH₃ < en < bipy < phen < NO₂⁻ < PPh₃ < CN⁻ < CO

Crystal field
Octahedral: t2g at −0.4Δo, eg at +0.6Δo per electron · Tetrahedral: Δt = (4/9)Δo, e at −0.6Δt, t₂ at +0.4Δt
Δo > pairing energy P ⇒ low spin (strong field); Δo < P ⇒ high spin
Colour arises from d–d transitions — [Ti(H₂O)₆]³⁺ is purple (d¹)

Stability & isomerism
Chelate effect: polydentate ligands (en, EDTA — hexadentate) form extra-stable complexes
Geometrical: cis/trans, fac/mer · Optical: non-superimposable mirror images (e.g., cis-[Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺) · Linkage (NO₂⁻/ONO⁻), ionisation, coordination and solvate isomerism

capsules.subject: Formula Handbook
capsules.title: Formula Handbook — Chemistry: Electrochemistry
capsules.body:
Cell potential
E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode · ΔG° = −nFE°cell
At 298 K: E°cell = (0.0591/n) log Kc · Nernst: E = E° − (0.0591/n) log Q
Standard hydrogen electrode = 0.00 V · Daniell cell E° = 1.10 V

Faraday’s laws
w = Z × Q = (M/nF) × i × t · 1 F = 96,500 C (= charge on 1 mol of electrons)
Same charge deposits masses in proportion to equivalent weights

Conductance
κ = (1/R) × (l/A) · Molar conductivity Λm = κ × 1000/c
Strong electrolytes: Λm = Λ°m − k√c · Weak: degree of dissociation α = Λm/Λ°m
Kohlrausch: Λ° = ν₊λ°₊ + ν₋λ°₋ (each ion migrates independently at infinite dilution)

capsules.subject: Formula Handbook
capsules.title: Formula Handbook — Chemistry: GOC & Name Reactions map
capsules.body:
Electronic effects
+I order: (CH₃)₃C− > (CH₃)₂CH− > C₂H₅− > CH₃− > H · −I order: −NO₂ > −CN > −COOH > −F > −Cl > −Br > −I
Carbocation stability: resonance > 3° > 2° > 1° (hyperconjugation + +I); carbanion order is the reverse
Acid strength rises with −I groups near −COOH; aqueous basicity of ethyl amines: 2° > 1° > 3° > NH₃; aniline is far weaker (lone pair delocalised)

Name reactions — one line each
Wurtz: 2RX + Na → alkane (dry ether) · Kolbe electrolysis: carboxylate → alkane + CO₂ at anode
HVZ: α-halogenation of acids (P/X₂) · Haloform: CHI₃ from methyl ketones / ethanol with I₂/NaOH
Cannizzaro: aldehydes without α-H → alcohol + acid · Aldol: aldehydes with α-H, dil. NaOH
Clemmensen: Zn(Hg)/HCl reduces C=O to CH₂ · Wolff–Kishner: NH₂NH₂/KOH does the same (basic medium)
Hoffmann bromamide: amide → amine with one C less (Br₂/NaOH) · Carbylamine: 1° amine + CHCl₃/KOH → foul isocyanide
Sandmeyer / Gattermann: diazonium → aryl halides · Diazotisation: aniline + NaNO₂/HCl, 273–278 K
Kolbe–Schmitt: phenol + CO₂ → salicylic acid · Reimer–Tiemann: phenol + CHCl₃/KOH → salicylaldehyde
Rosenmund: acid chloride + H₂/Pd–BaSO₄ → aldehyde · Stephen: nitrile + SnCl₂/HCl → aldehyde · Etard: toluene CrO₂Cl₂ → benzaldehyde
Gabriel phthalimide: pure 1° aliphatic amines · Williamson: ether from alkoxide + alkyl halide (SN2 — use 1° halide)

capsules.subject: Formula Handbook
capsules.title: Formula Handbook — Maths: Definite Integration & Area
capsules.body:
Core results
∫ab f(x)dx = F(b) − F(a) · King’s property: ∫ab f(x)dx = ∫ab f(a + b − x)dx
∫−aa f = 2∫0a f if f is even; = 0 if f is odd · ∫02a f = 2∫0a f if f(2a − x) = f(x)
Leibniz: d/dx ∫a(x)b(x) f(t)dt = f(b(x))·b′(x) − f(a(x))·a′(x)

Standards to memorise
∫ dx/(x² + a²) = (1/a) tan⁻¹(x/a) · ∫ dx/√(a² − x²) = sin⁻¹(x/a) · ∫ dx/(a² − x²) = (1/2a) ln|(a + x)/(a − x)|
∫ √(a² − x²) dx = (x/2)√(a² − x²) + (a²/2) sin⁻¹(x/a) · ∫ ex(f + f′)dx = exf(x)
Walli’s formula: ∫0π/2 sinⁿx dx — multiply odd/even chains (n−1)/n · (n−3)/(n−2)…, × π/2 only when n is even

Areas
Between curves: ∫ (ytop − ybottom) dx · With the y-axis: ∫ x dy · Ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1: area = πab
Use symmetry before integrating — half of all area questions collapse with one sketch

capsules.subject: Formula Handbook
capsules.title: Formula Handbook — Maths: Vectors & 3D Geometry
capsules.body:
Vectors
a·b = |a||b| cosθ (θ = angle between them); a ⊥ b ⇔ a·b = 0 · Projection of a on b = (a·b)/|b|
|a × b| = |a||b| sinθ = area of parallelogram with sides a, b (triangle = half)
Scalar triple product [a b c] = volume of parallelepiped; tetrahedron = (1/6)|[a b c]|; coplanar ⇔ [a b c] = 0

Lines
r = a + λb · Angle between two lines: cosθ = |b₁·b₂| / (|b₁||b₂|)
Shortest distance between skew lines: |(a₂ − a₁)·(b₁ × b₂)| / |b₁ × b₂| · Parallel lines: |(a₂ − a₁) × b| / |b|

Planes
ax + by + cz + d = 0, normal (a, b, c) · Distance of point (x₁, y₁, z₁): |ax₁ + by₁ + cz₁ + d| / √(a² + b² + c²)
Angle between line and plane: sinθ = |b·n| / (|b||n|) · Angle between planes = angle between normals
Plane through intersection of two planes: P₁ + λP₂ = 0

capsules.subject: Formula Handbook
capsules.title: Formula Handbook — Maths: Probability
capsules.body:
Rules
P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B); if mutually exclusive, just add
Conditional: P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B) · Multiplication: P(A ∩ B) = P(A)·P(B|A)
Independent events: P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B) — always verify, never assume
Total probability: P(A) = Σ P(Bᵢ)·P(A|Bᵢ) · Bayes: P(Bᵢ|A) = P(Bᵢ)P(A|Bᵢ) / Σ P(Bⱼ)P(A|Bⱼ)

Binomial distribution
P(X = r) = ⁿCr pr qn−r (q = 1 − p) · Mean = np · Variance = npq · SD = √(npq)
Most likely value (mode) ≈ np

Random variables
E(X) = Σ xᵢpᵢ · Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]² · E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b · Σ pᵢ = 1 always — use it to find unknown constants

capsules.subject: Formula Handbook
capsules.title: Formula Handbook — Maths: Matrices & Determinants
capsules.body:
Inverse & transpose
A⁻¹ = (adj A)/|A| (exists ⇔ |A| ≠ 0) · (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹ · (Aᵀ)⁻¹ = (A⁻¹)ᵀ · adj(adj A) = |A|n−2 A
Symmetric: Aᵀ = A · Skew-symmetric: Aᵀ = −A (diagonal entries all zero) · Every square matrix = symmetric + skew-symmetric
Orthogonal: AAᵀ = I ⇒ |A| = ±1

Determinant properties
|kA| = kⁿ|A| (n = order) · |AB| = |A||B| · |Aᵀ| = |A| · Swapping two rows flips the sign; identical rows ⇒ 0
Area of a triangle = (1/2)|x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|; collinear ⇔ area 0

Systems AX = B
|A| ≠ 0 ⇒ unique solution (Cramer: x = Dx/D, …) · |A| = 0 and (adj A)B ≠ 0 ⇒ no solution · |A| = 0 and (adj A)B = 0 ⇒ either no solution or infinitely many — check a principal minor/rank before concluding

capsules.subject: Exam Info
capsules.title: JEE Main chapter-wise weightage — where the marks sit (indicative)
capsules.body:
Compiled from previous-10-year JEE Main paper analyses. Treat these as indicative ranges to prioritise revision — NTA does not publish official weightages, and every chapter still draws questions.

Physics (high-yield first) — Modern Physics ≈ 9–10% · Optics ≈ 8–9% · Current Electricity ≈ 7–8% · Electrostatics ≈ 7% · Thermodynamics & KTG ≈ 7% · Rotational Motion ≈ 6–7% · Magnetism & EMI/AC together ≈ 10% · Mechanics (NLM + WPE + COM) ≈ 10–12%

Chemistry — Organic overall ≈ 30% (GOC + reaction mechanisms are the base layer) · Coordination Compounds ≈ 7% · Chemical Bonding ≈ 6–7% · Electrochemistry ≈ 5% · Chemical & Ionic Equilibrium ≈ 7–8% · Thermodynamics ≈ 5% · p-Block + d/f-Block (NCERT-heavy) ≈ 10%

Maths — Vectors & 3D ≈ 9–11% · Matrices & Determinants ≈ 7% · Definite Integration & Area ≈ 7–8% · Probability ≈ 6% · Sequences & Series ≈ 6% · Limits, Continuity, Differentiability + Application of Derivatives ≈ 10% · Straight Lines & Circles ≈ 7%

How to use this: revise in weightage order with the Formula Handbook capsules, then close each chapter with previous-year questions. High weightage × high accuracy is where ranks are made.
