capsules.subject: Physics
capsules.title: Atomic clocks keep NavIC ticking (science in news)
capsules.body: NavIC stopped giving location data partly because of atomic-clock failures. JEE angle: navigation needs nanosecond timing — a 1 μs error = ~300 m position error (c = 3×108 m/s). Caesium/rubidium clocks use the hyperfine-transition frequency as the standard; frequency stability (Δf/f) maps directly to timing error. NVS-03 (30 Oct 2026) aims to restore the 4-satellite minimum.

oneliners.text: Range of a projectile on level ground: R = u²sin2θ/g, maximum at θ = 45°.
Projectile time of flight T = 2u sinθ/g; maximum height H = u²sin²θ/g.
Centripetal force F = mv²/r = mω²r; centripetal acceleration a = v²/r directed toward the centre.
Newton's law of gravitation: F = Gm₁m₂/r²; G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg².
g at height h (h ≪ R): g_h = g(1 − 2h/R); at depth d: g_d = g(1 − d/R).
Escape velocity v_e = √(2GM/R) = √(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km/s for Earth.
Orbital velocity near Earth's surface v_o = √(gR) ≈ 7.92 km/s; escape velocity = √2 × orbital velocity.
Kepler's third law: T² ∝ r³ — square of orbital period proportional to cube of orbital radius.
Power P = F·v = dW/dt; 1 horsepower ≈ 746 W.
Elastic potential energy U = ½kx²; spring restoring force F = −kx.
Elastic collision of equal masses in 1D: the bodies exchange velocities.
Coefficient of restitution e = (relative speed after)/(relative speed before); e = 1 elastic, e = 0 perfectly inelastic.
Centre of mass of a uniform semicircular wire is at 2R/π from the centre along its axis of symmetry.
Moments of inertia: ring MR², disc ½MR², solid sphere ⅖MR², hollow sphere ⅔MR², rod about centre (1/12)ML².
Parallel-axis theorem I = I_cm + Md²; perpendicular-axis theorem I_z = I_x + I_y for a plane lamina.
Torque τ = r × F; angular momentum L = r × p = Iω; τ = dL/dt.
Rolling without slipping: v_cm = ωR; total KE = ½mv² + ½Iω².
Acceleration rolling down an incline: a = g sinθ/(1 + I/mR²).
Geostationary satellite: period 24 h, height ≈ 36,000 km, orbits in the equatorial plane west to east.
Apparent weight in a lift: N = m(g + a) accelerating up, m(g − a) accelerating down, zero in free fall.
Banking angle tanθ = v²/(rg); maximum speed on an unbanked curve v_max = √(μ_s rg).
Minimum speed to complete a vertical circle: √(gr) at the top, √(5gr) at the bottom; tension is maximum at the bottom.
Conical pendulum: tanθ = ω²r/g; period T = 2π√(l cosθ/g).
Static friction is self-adjusting up to f_s ≤ μ_s N; kinetic friction f_k = μ_k N opposes relative motion.
Stokes' law F = 6πηrv; terminal velocity of a falling sphere v_t = 2r²g(ρ − σ)/(9η).
Bernoulli: P + ½ρv² + ρgh = constant along a streamline for steady incompressible flow.
Continuity A₁v₁ = A₂v₂; Torricelli efflux speed v = √(2gh).
Capillary rise h = 2Tcosθ/(ρgr); excess pressure: liquid drop 2T/R, soap bubble 4T/R.
Young's modulus Y = stress/strain = (F/A)/(ΔL/L); Hooke's law holds up to the elastic limit.
Bulk modulus K = −P/(ΔV/V); shear (rigidity) modulus η = shear stress/shear strain.
Poisson's ratio σ = −(lateral strain)/(longitudinal strain); theoretical range −1 to 0.5.
Linear expansion ΔL = αLΔT; volume expansion β = 3α for isotropic solids.
Newton's law of cooling: rate of cooling ∝ (T − T₀); temperature falls exponentially.
Stefan–Boltzmann E = σT⁴ (σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W/m²K⁴); Wien's displacement λ_m T = 2.9 × 10⁻³ m·K.
Thermal conduction dQ/dt = −kA(dT/dx); good conductors have high thermal conductivity k.
Mayer's relation C_p − C_v = R; γ = C_p/C_v: monoatomic 5/3, diatomic 7/5, polyatomic 4/3.
Adiabatic: PV^γ = constant; TV^(γ−1) = constant; work W = (P₁V₁ − P₂V₂)/(γ − 1).
Isothermal work W = nRT ln(V₂/V₁); internal-energy change is zero for ideal-gas isothermal process.
Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T_C/T_H; no heat engine beats a Carnot engine between the same reservoirs.
Entropy change ΔS = ∫dQ_rev/T; entropy of the universe increases in every irreversible process.
Kinetic theory: PV = (1/3)Nm v_rms²; pressure arises from molecular collisions.
v_rms = √(3RT/M); v_rms : v_avg : v_mp = √3 : √(8/π) : √2.
Equipartition: (1/2)kT per quadratic degree of freedom; molar internal energy (f/2)RT.
SHM: a = −ω²x; x = A sin(ωt + φ); ω = √(k/m); T = 2π√(m/k).
Simple pendulum T = 2π√(l/g) — independent of bob mass and of small amplitude.
SHM total energy E = ½kA² = ½mω²A² is constant; KE peaks at mean position, PE at extremes.
Seconds pendulum: T = 2 s, length ≈ 1 m.
Resonance: oscillation amplitude peaks when the driving frequency matches the natural frequency.
Wave speed on a string v = √(T/μ); in general v = fλ.
String fixed at both ends: f_n = nv/(2L); open pipe f_n = nv/(2L); closed pipe f_n = (2n−1)v/(4L), odd harmonics only.
Beat frequency = |f₁ − f₂|; beats are heard when the two frequencies are close.
Doppler: f′ = f(v ± v_o)/(v ∓ v_s) — plus in the numerator when the observer moves toward the source.
Sound intensity level β = 10 log₁₀(I/I₀) dB; I₀ = 10⁻¹² W/m² is the threshold of hearing.
Coulomb's law F = kq₁q₂/r²; k = 1/(4πε₀) = 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C².
Electric dipole: torque τ = p × E; potential energy U = −p·E; axial field = 2kp/r³.
Gauss's law ∮E·dA = Q_enc/ε₀; field just outside a conductor's surface = σ/ε₀.
Field inside a uniformly charged spherical shell is zero; outside it behaves as a point charge.
Parallel-plate capacitance C = ε₀A/d; dielectric multiplies by K; series 1/C = Σ1/Cᵢ, parallel C = ΣCᵢ.
Capacitor energy U = ½CV² = Q²/2C; energy density = ½ε₀E².
Resistance R = ρl/A; R(T) = R₀[1 + α(T − T₀)]; drift velocity v_d = I/(neA).
Kirchhoff's laws: ΣI = 0 at a junction (charge conservation); ΣV = 0 around a loop (energy conservation).
Wheatstone bridge is balanced when P/Q = R/S; the galvanometer then carries no current.
Terminal voltage V = E − Ir; maximum power is delivered when load R equals internal resistance r.
Biot–Savart: dB = (μ₀/4π)I dl×r̂/r²; field of a long straight wire B = μ₀I/(2πr).
Field at the centre of a circular loop B = μ₀I/(2R); of an arc subtending angle θ: B = μ₀Iθ/(4πR).
Solenoid B = μ₀nI inside (μ₀nI/2 at the ends); toroid B = μ₀NI/(2πr).
Lorentz force F = q(E + v × B); a charge in perpendicular B moves in a circle of radius r = mv/(qB).
Cyclotron frequency f = qB/(2πm) is independent of speed; KE_max = q²B²R²/(2m).
Force per unit length between parallel wires F/l = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd); attractive for parallel currents.
Field on the axis of a current loop: B = μ₀IR²/[2(R²+x²)^(3/2)] — reduces to μ₀I/(2R) at the centre.
Galvanometer → ammeter with a low-resistance shunt in parallel; → voltmeter with a high resistance in series.
Faraday ε = −N dΦ_B/dt; Lenz's law: the induced current opposes the change producing it.
Motional EMF ε = Blv for a rod cutting field lines perpendicularly.
Solenoid inductance L = μ₀n²Al; inductor energy U = ½LI²; induced EMF ε = −L dI/dt.
LR current growth I = I₀(1 − e^(−Rt/L)); RC charging Q = Q₀(1 − e^(−t/RC)); time constants L/R and RC.
LC circuit oscillates at f = 1/(2π√(LC)); energy shuttles between capacitor and inductor.
AC averages: V_rms = V₀/√2; average power P = V_rms I_rms cosφ (cosφ = power factor).
Series RLC resonates at f₀ = 1/(2π√(LC)): X_L = X_C, impedance minimum (= R), current maximum.
Reactances X_L = ωL, X_C = 1/(ωC); impedance Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²).
Transformer V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p = I_p/I_s; works only on AC.
EM waves: c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀) ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s; E ⊥ B ⊥ propagation direction; E₀/B₀ = c.
EM spectrum by increasing wavelength: γ-rays, X-rays, UV, visible, IR, microwaves, radio waves.
A coin under water appears raised: observed depth = real depth/n; a glass slab shifts rays laterally by t(1 − 1/n).
Lensmaker 1/f = (n−1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂); lens power P = 1/f in dioptres; lenses in contact P = P₁ + P₂.
Prism minimum deviation n = sin((A+δ_m)/2)/sin(A/2); thin prism δ = (n−1)A.
Cauchy dispersion n = A + B/λ²: violet (short λ) deviates most, red least.
Young's double slit fringe width β = λD/d; bright fringes at path difference nλ.
Single-slit minima at a sinθ = nλ; central maximum angular width = 2λ/a.
Rayleigh: telescope resolves θ ≥ 1.22λ/D; microscope d_min = 1.22λ/(2NA).
Brewster tanθ_B = n₂/n₁ gives fully polarized reflected light; Malus' law I = I₀cos²θ.
Mole relations: n = mass/M = N/N_A; Avogadro constant N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
Molarity = mol per litre of solution; molality = mol per kg of solvent; mole fraction x₁ = n₁/(n₁ + n₂).
Ideal gas PV = nRT; R = 8.314 J/mol·K = 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K; 1 mol occupies 22.4 L at STP.
Dalton P_total = ΣP_i; Graham r₁/r₂ = √(M₂/M₁) — lighter gases diffuse faster.
van der Waals (P + an²/V²)(V − nb) = nRT; a corrects for attraction, b for molecular volume.
Compressibility Z = PV/(nRT); Z = 1 for an ideal gas; Boyle temperature T_b = a/(Rb).
Planck E = hν; h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s.
Quantum numbers: n = 1, 2, …; l = 0 to n−1; m = −l to +l; s = ±½; maximum electrons in shell n is 2n².
Aufbau (n+l) rule; Pauli exclusion principle; Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity.
Anomalous configurations Cr [Ar]3d⁵4s¹ and Cu [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ come from half/full-filled subshell stability.
Nodes: radial = n − l − 1, angular = l, total = n − 1.
Ionization energy rises across a period, falls down a group; second IE always exceeds the first.
Electron affinity order: Cl > F > Br > I (F anomalously low from small size); noble gases ≈ 0.
Electronegativity: F highest at 4.0 (Pauling); rises across a period, falls down a group.
Atomic/ionic radius falls across a period, rises down a group; cations are smaller and anions larger than the parent atom.
Bond order = ½(N_b − N_a); higher bond order means a shorter, stronger bond.
VSEPR repulsion order lp–lp > lp–bp > bp–bp governs molecular shapes.
Bond angles shrink with lone pairs: CH₄ 109.5° > NH₃ 107° > H₂O 104.5° (VSEPR lone-pair repulsion).
O₂ is paramagnetic (two unpaired π* electrons) — explained only by molecular orbital theory.
N₂ has bond order 3; CO is isoelectronic with N₂.
Hydrogen-bond strength HF > H₂O > NH₃; explains the anomalously high boiling points of HF and H₂O.
Dipole moment μ = q × d; CO₂ has zero dipole (linear, symmetric), H₂O has 1.85 D.
Fajans' rules: small highly-charged cation + large anion → greater covalent character.
Lattice energy ∝ (z⁺z⁻)/(r⁺ + r⁻) (Born–Landé).
Hess's law: ΔH_rxn = ΣΔH_f(products) − ΣΔH_f(reactants); enthalpy is a state function.
Bond-enthalpy estimate: ΔH ≈ Σ(bonds broken) − Σ(bonds formed).
ΔG = ΔH − TΔS; spontaneous when ΔG < 0; at equilibrium ΔG = 0.
ΔG° = −RT ln K = −nFE°; at 298 K, log K = nE°/0.0591.
Entropy order S_gas > S_liquid > S_solid; ΔS_universe > 0 for spontaneous processes.
Rate = k[A]^m[B]^n; order (m+n) is experimental, molecularity is theoretical.
First order: k = (2.303/t)log([A]₀/[A]); t½ = 0.693/k, independent of initial concentration.
Zero order: [A] = [A]₀ − kt; t½ = [A]₀/(2k); rate independent of concentration.
Second order (single reactant): 1/[A] = 1/[A]₀ + kt; t½ = 1/(k[A]₀).
Arrhenius k = Ae^(−E_a/RT); a 10 K temperature rise roughly doubles the reaction rate.
A catalyst lowers activation energy, speeds forward and reverse equally, and leaves K and ΔG unchanged.
K_p = K_c(RT)^Δn_g; the equilibrium constant depends only on temperature.
Le Chatelier: higher pressure favours fewer gas moles; higher temperature favours the endothermic side.
pH = −log[H⁺]; pH + pOH = 14 at 25 °C; K_w = 10⁻¹⁴.
Henderson–Hasselbalch: pH = pK_a + log([salt]/[acid]) for buffer solutions.
Weak-acid dissociation α = √(K_a/c) (Ostwald's dilution law).
Precipitation begins when the ionic product exceeds K_sp; for A_xB_y, K_sp = [A]^x[B]^y.
Common-ion effect suppresses weak-electrolyte dissociation and salt solubility.
Salt of weak acid + strong base hydrolyses basic (pH > 7); weak base + strong acid hydrolyses acidic.
E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode; the cell is spontaneous when E°cell > 0.
Nernst at 298 K: E = E° − (0.0591/n)log Q.
Faraday's laws: w = (E × I × t)/96500; 1 faraday = 96485 C per mole of electrons.
Standard hydrogen electrode is assigned E° = 0.00 V as the reference.
Kohlrausch: Λ_m° = ν₊λ₊° + ν₋λ₋°; molar conductivity Λ_m = κ × 1000/M.
Coordination: oxidation state = primary valency; coordination number = secondary valency.
Octahedral crystal-field splitting: t₂g lower, e_g upper by Δ_o; tetrahedral Δ_t = (4/9)Δ_o.
Spectrochemical series (weak → strong): I⁻ < Br⁻ < Cl⁻ < F⁻ < OH⁻ < H₂O < NH₃ < en < NO₂⁻ < CN⁻ < CO.
Low spin when Δ_o > pairing energy P; high spin when Δ_o < P.
CFT examples: high-spin d⁵ (weak field) has 5 unpaired electrons (μ = 5.92 BM); low-spin d⁶ has none.
Chelate effect: multidentate ligands form extra-stable complexes; EDTA is hexadentate.
Linkage isomerism: NO₂⁻ as nitro (N-bound) vs nitrito (O-bound).
Ionization isomers: [Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Br and [Co(NH₃)₅Br]SO₄.
Zn, Cd, Hg are d-block but not transition elements (d¹⁰ in ground and common oxidation states).
5f orbitals shield more poorly than 4f, so the size decrease across actinides is larger than across lanthanides.
KMnO₄ in acid oxidizes Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺, oxalate → CO₂, and SO₂ → sulfate; it is its own indicator.
Acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ oxidizes ethanol to ethanal and then ethanoic acid (orange → green); basis of the breathalyzer.
Alloys: brass Cu+Zn, bronze Cu+Sn, German silver Cu+Zn+Ni, steel Fe+C.
Inert-pair effect: heavier p-block elements favour the lower oxidation state (Pb²⁺ stabler than Pb⁴⁺).
Borax Na₂B₄O₇·10H₂O; boric acid is a weak monobasic Lewis acid.
Graphite (sp² layers) conducts electricity; diamond (sp³ network) is the hardest natural insulator.
Fullerene C₆₀: 12 pentagons + 20 hexagons (buckminsterfullerene).
Haber: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ (Fe, ~450 °C, ~200 atm); Contact: 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ (V₂O₅).
Halogen oxidizing power: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂.
First noble-gas compound XePtF₆ (Bartlett, 1962); xenon also forms XeF₂, XeF₄, XeF₆.
Flame colours: Li crimson, Na golden yellow, K lilac, Ca brick red, Sr crimson, Ba apple green.
Diagonal relationships: Li–Mg, Be–Al, B–Si show similar properties.
Temporary hardness (Ca/Mg bicarbonates) is removed by boiling; permanent hardness (chlorides/sulfates) needs ion exchange.
Functional-group priority: COOH > anhydride > ester > COCl > amide > CN > CHO > ketone > alcohol > amine.
Markovnikov: H adds to the carbon with more hydrogens, via the more stable carbocation.
Peroxide effect: HBr + ROOR adds Br to the less substituted carbon — unique to HBr.
Carbocation stability 3° > 2° > 1° > methyl; rearranges by hydride or methyl shift.
SN1: rate = k[RX], 3° fastest, racemization; SN2: rate = k[RX][Nu⁻], 1° fastest, inversion (Walden).
Saytzeff: the more substituted alkene dominates in elimination; bulky base gives the Hofmann (less substituted) alkene.
Grignard RMgX: + formaldehyde → 1° alcohol; + other aldehydes → 2°; + ketones → 3°.
Aldol: α-H carbonyl + dil. NaOH → β-hydroxy carbonyl, which dehydrates to an α,β-unsaturated carbonyl.
Cannizzaro: aldehydes lacking α-H + conc. KOH disproportionate to alcohol + carboxylate.
Iodoform test: CH₃CO– or CH₃CH(OH)– groups give yellow CHI₃ with I₂/NaOH.
Tollens' (silver mirror) and Fehling's (red Cu₂O) detect aldehydes; ketones do not reduce them.
Rosenmund RCOCl → RCHO (Pd/BaSO₄); Clemmensen and Wolff–Kishner reduce C=O to CH₂.
o/p directors: –OH, –NH₂, –OR, –R, halogens; m directors: –NO₂, –CN, –CHO, –COOH, –SO₃H.
Sandmeyer: ArN₂⁺Cl⁻ + CuCl/CuBr/CuCN → ArCl/ArBr/ArCN (diazotization at 0–5 °C first).
Quadratic D = b² − 4ac: > 0 real distinct roots, = 0 equal roots, < 0 complex conjugate roots.
Vieta: quadratic sum = −b/a, product = c/a; cubic: Σ = −b/a, Σ pairwise = c/a, product = −d/a.
AM ≥ GM ≥ HM for positive numbers; equality iff all numbers are equal.
GM² = AM × HM for two positive numbers.
Binomial (x+y)^n = Σ ⁿC_r x^(n−r)y^r; ⁿC_r = ⁿC_(n−r); n even → one middle term, n odd → two.
Σ ⁿC_r = 2^n; alternating sum Σ(−1)^r ⁿC_r = 0.
Pascal's identity: ⁿC_r + ⁿC_(r−1) = ⁿ⁺¹C_r.
(AB)^T = B^T A^T; (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹; |AB| = |A||B|.
A⁻¹ = adj(A)/|A|; A·adj(A) = |A|I; singular iff |A| = 0.
|kA| = k^n|A| for n×n; swapping two rows flips the determinant's sign.
Cramer's rule: x = D_x/D, y = D_y/D for D ≠ 0.
sin(A±B) = sinAcosB ± cosAsinB; cos(A±B) = cosAcosB ∓ sinAsinB.
tan(A+B) = (tanA + tanB)/(1 − tanA tanB).
sin2A = 2sinAcosA; cos2A = 2cos²A − 1 = 1 − 2sin²A; tan2A = 2tanA/(1 − tan²A).
sin3A = 3sinA − 4sin³A; cos3A = 4cos³A − 3cosA.
Maximum of a sinx + b cosx is √(a²+b²); minimum is −√(a²+b²).
Sine rule: a/sinA = b/sinB = c/sinC = 2R.
Cosine rule c² = a² + b² − 2ab cosC; projection formula a = b cosC + c cosB.
Triangle area: Δ = ½bc sinA = abc/(4R) = rs = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)].
R = abc/(4Δ); r = Δ/s; Euler OI² = R(R − 2r).
sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x = π/2; tan⁻¹x + cot⁻¹x = π/2; sec⁻¹x + cosec⁻¹x = π/2.
tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y = tan⁻¹((x+y)/(1−xy)) for xy < 1.
2tan⁻¹x = sin⁻¹(2x/(1+x²)) = cos⁻¹((1−x²)/(1+x²)) = tan⁻¹(2x/(1−x²)).
lim(x→0) sinx/x = 1; lim(x→0)(e^x−1)/x = 1; lim(x→0) ln(1+x)/x = 1; lim(x→0)(a^x−1)/x = ln a.
L'Hôpital applies to 0/0 and ∞/∞ forms: differentiate numerator and denominator separately.
Rolle: f(a) = f(b) with continuity/differentiability ⇒ f′(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b).
LMVT: f′(c) = (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a) for some c in (a,b).
d/dx[x^n] = nx^(n−1); d/dx[e^x] = e^x; d/dx[lnx] = 1/x; d/dx[a^x] = a^x ln a.
(uv)′ = u′v + uv′; (u/v)′ = (u′v − uv′)/v²; chain rule dy/dx = dy/du · du/dx.
d/dx[sin⁻¹x] = 1/√(1−x²); d/dx[tan⁻¹x] = 1/(1+x²); d/dx[sec⁻¹x] = 1/(|x|√(x²−1)).
If f′ switches sign from + to − at a critical point it is a local maximum; from − to + a local minimum.
∫x^n dx = x^(n+1)/(n+1) (n ≠ −1); ∫dx/x = ln|x|; ∫e^x dx = e^x.
∫sec²x dx = tanx; ∫cosec²x dx = −cotx; ∫secx tanx dx = secx.
∫dx/(1+x²) = tan⁻¹x; ∫dx/√(1−x²) = sin⁻¹x.
∫√(a²−x²)dx = (x/2)√(a²−x²) + (a²/2)sin⁻¹(x/a).
Integration by parts ∫u dv = uv − ∫v du; choose u by ILATE order.
King's property: ∫₀^a f(x)dx = ∫₀^a f(a−x)dx.
∫₋ₐ^a f = 2∫₀^a f if f is even, 0 if f is odd.
∫₀^(π/2) sin^n x dx = ∫₀^(π/2) cos^n x dx (Wallis reduction).
∫₀^π x f(sin x)dx = (π/2)∫₀^π f(sin x)dx.
Area = ∫(top − bottom)dx; volume about the x-axis V = π∫y²dx.
Order = highest derivative; degree = power of the highest derivative (after clearing radicals).
Variable separable: dy/dx = f(x)g(y) ⇒ ∫dy/g(y) = ∫f(x)dx + c.
Linear DE dy/dx + Py = Q: IF = e^∫Pdx; solution y·IF = ∫Q·IF dx + c.
a·b = |a||b|cosθ; |a×b| = |a||b|sinθ; (a×b)² + (a·b)² = |a|²|b|² (Lagrange identity).
Scalar triple product [abc] = volume of the parallelepiped; zero iff vectors are coplanar.
a×(b×c) = (a·c)b − (a·b)c.
A line making angles α, β, γ with the axes satisfies cos²α + cos²β + cos²γ = 1.
Skew-line distance = |(a₂−a₁)·(b₁×b₂)|/|b₁×b₂|.
Intercept form of a plane: x/a + y/b + z/c = 1; normal form: lx + my + nz = p.
P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A∩B); P(A|B) = P(A∩B)/P(B).
Bayes: P(E_i|A) = P(E_i)P(A|E_i)/Σ_j P(E_j)P(A|E_j).
Independent ⇔ P(A∩B) = P(A)P(B); mutually exclusive ⇔ P(A∩B) = 0.
Binomial P(X=r) = ⁿC_r p^r q^(n−r); mean np, variance npq.
Variance = E[X²] − (E[X])²; SD = √variance.
ⁿP_r = n!/(n−r)!; ⁿC_r = n!/(r!(n−r)!); circular permutations = (n−1)!.
|z₁z₂| = |z₁||z₂|; arg(z₁z₂) = arg z₁ + arg z₂; z·z̄ = |z|².
Cube roots of unity: 1, ω, ω² with ω³ = 1 and 1 + ω + ω² = 0.
De Moivre: (cosθ + i sinθ)^n = cos nθ + i sin nθ.
Triangle inequalities: |z₁+z₂| ≤ |z₁|+|z₂|; ||z₁|−|z₂|| ≤ |z₁−z₂|.
Parabola y² = 4ax: focus (a,0), directrix x = −a, latus rectum 4a, e = 1.
Ellipse: e = √(1−b²/a²) < 1, foci (±ae,0), latus rectum 2b²/a.
Hyperbola: e > 1, asymptotes y = ±(b/a)x; rectangular hyperbola xy = c² has e = √2.
Circle x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c = 0: centre (−g,−f), radius √(g²+f²−c).
Tangent T = 0; chord of contact T = 0; chord with given midpoint T = S₁; pair of tangents SS₁ = T².
Parametric: circle (a cosθ, a sinθ); ellipse (a cosθ, b sinθ); parabola (at², 2at); hyperbola (a secθ, b tanθ).
Section formula (internal): ((mx₂+nx₁)/(m+n), (my₂+ny₁)/(m+n)); perpendicular lines m₁m₂ = −1.
Line forms: y = mx + c; x/a + y/b = 1; x cosα + y sinα = p.
Distance between parallel lines ax+by+c₁ = 0 and ax+by+c₂ = 0 is |c₁−c₂|/√(a²+b²).
log_a(xy) = log_a x + log_a y; log_a x^n = n log_a x; change of base log_a b = ln b/ln a.
Escape velocity from Earth ≈ 11.2 km/s; from the Moon ≈ 2.38 km/s.
Geostationary orbit radius ≈ 42,200 km from Earth's centre (≈ 35,800 km altitude).
Orbital speed of a low-Earth-orbit satellite ≈ 7.9 km/s (first cosmic velocity).
Kepler's third law: T² ∝ r³ for planetary orbits.
Variation of g with height h: g′ = g/(1 + h/R)²; with depth d: g′ = g(1 − d/R).
g is maximum at the poles and minimum at the equator.
Gravitational potential V = −GM/r; potential energy U = −GMm/r.
A satellite's total mechanical energy = −GMm/(2r) (negative, half the potential energy).
Binding energy of a satellite = +GMm/(2r).
Weightlessness in orbit is free fall, not the absence of gravity.
Centripetal force does no work — it stays perpendicular to velocity.
In uniform circular motion speed is constant but velocity and acceleration keep changing direction.
Banking angle for a frictionless turn: tan θ = v²/(rg).
Conical pendulum: T = 2π√(L cos θ/g).
In a vertical circle, tension at the bottom exceeds tension at the top by 6mg.
Minimum speed at the top of a vertical loop to stay on track: √(gR).
Mean free path λ = 1/(√2 n π d²) — inversely proportional to the square of molecular diameter.
Degrees of freedom: monatomic 3, diatomic 5 (room T), nonlinear polyatomic 6.
γ = Cp/Cv: 5/3 (monatomic), 7/5 (diatomic), 4/3 (polyatomic).
Maxwell speeds: v_mp : v_avg : v_rms = 1 : 1.128 : 1.225.
Graham's law: rate of effusion ∝ 1/√M.
Internal energy of n moles of ideal gas: U = (f/2)nRT.
Pressure of an ideal gas = (2/3) × translational kinetic energy per unit volume.
Real gases deviate most from ideal behaviour at high pressure and low temperature.
Boyle temperature: the temperature at which a real gas obeys Boyle's law over a wide pressure range.
Average velocity over any closed loop is zero; average speed is not.
Slope of x–t graph = velocity; slope of v–t = acceleration; area under v–t = displacement; area under a–t = Δv.
Stopping distance ∝ (initial speed)² under constant deceleration.
Distance travelled in the nth second: s_n = u + a(2n−1)/2.
Relative velocity: v_AB = v_A − v_B (vector subtraction).
Parallelogram identity: |a + b|² + |a − b|² = 2(|a|² + |b|²).
a · b = |a||b|cos θ; |a × b| = |a||b|sin θ with direction by the right-hand rule.
Scalar triple product [a b c] = 0 ⟺ the three vectors are coplanar.
Unit vector in the direction of r: r̂ = r/|r|.
Discriminant of ax² + bx + c: D = b² − 4ac; D > 0 two real roots, D = 0 equal roots, D < 0 complex conjugate pair.
For ax² + bx + c = 0: sum of roots = −b/a, product of roots = c/a.
If α, β are the roots, the quadratic is x² − (α + β)x + αβ = 0.
ax² + bx + c > 0 for all x ⟺ a > 0 and D < 0.
Between the roots a quadratic takes the sign opposite to a; outside the roots it takes the sign of a.
A quadratic attains its extremum at x = −b/(2a).
If one root of ax² + bx + c = 0 is the reciprocal of the other, then a = c.
Slope of the tangent = dy/dx evaluated at the point of contact.
Tangent at (x₁, y₁) on y = f(x): y − y₁ = f′(x₁)(x − x₁).
Normal is perpendicular to the tangent; slope of normal = −1/f′(x₁).
A function increases where f′(x) > 0 and decreases where f′(x) < 0.
Critical points: f′(x) = 0 or f′ undefined; second-derivative test: f″ > 0 minima, f″ < 0 maxima.
Rolle's theorem: f continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b), f(a) = f(b) ⟹ f′(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b).
Cauchy's mean value theorem: (f(b) − f(a))/(g(b) − g(a)) = f′(c)/g′(c) for some c in (a,b).
For a sphere: dV/dt = 4πr² dr/dt.
Linear approximation: f(x + Δx) ≈ f(x) + f′(x)Δx.
∫ f′(x)/f(x) dx = ln|f(x)| + C.
Order = highest derivative present; degree = power of the highest derivative after clearing radicals and fractions.
Bernoulli's equation dy/dx + Py = Qyⁿ: substitute v = y^{1−n} to linearise it.
Linear DE dy/dx + Py = Q: integrating factor = e^{∫P dx}.
Homogeneous DE: substitute y = vx to make it separable.
Orthogonal trajectories: replace dy/dx by −dx/dy and solve.
The DE of the family y = Ae^{mx} + Be^{−mx} is d²y/dx² = m²y.
One-one functions from an m-element set to an n-element set (m ≤ n): P(n, m).
Onto functions from an n-element set to a 2-element set: 2ⁿ − 2.
Bijections of an n-element set: n! in number.
Reflexive relations on an n-element set: 2^{n²−n}.
Symmetric relations on an n-element set: 2^{n(n+1)/2}.
Equivalence relations on {1, 2, 3}: 5 (Bell number B₃).
fog ≠ gof in general; (fog)⁻¹ = g⁻¹ ∘ f⁻¹.
A function has an inverse ⟺ it is bijective.
n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B).
∫₀^{2a} f(x) dx = 2∫₀^a f(x) dx if f(2a − x) = f(x); it is 0 if f(2a − x) = −f(x).
Effective nuclear charge Z* = Z − σ (Slater's rules); rises across a period.
Atomic radius falls across a period (rising Z*) and grows down a group (new shells).
Isoelectronic species: size falls as nuclear charge rises.
First ionisation energy generally rises across a period and falls down a group.
IE anomalies: Be > B and N > O (stable filled/half-filled subshells); Mg > Al, P > S.
Electron affinity is most exothermic for Cl — fluorine's small size repels the added electron.
Electronegativity rises across a period and falls down a group; F is the most electronegative (4.0).
Metallic character grows down a group and shrinks across a period.
Amphoteric oxides: Al₂O₃, ZnO, BeO, PbO — they react with both acids and bases.
Diagonal relationship: Li resembles Mg; Be resembles Al.
Oxidising power of halogens: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂; reducing power of halides reverses.
Xe and Kr form fluorides and oxides (XeF₂, XeF₄, XeF₆, XeO₃).
Lanthanide contraction: steady radius shrink across the 4f series from poor 4f shielding.
Transition metals show variable oxidation states — both (n−1)d and ns electrons participate.
Highest common oxidation state +7 (Mn); Os and Ru reach +8.
The rate law is experimental — it is never written from the balanced equation.
Order can be zero, fractional or negative; molecularity is always a positive integer.
Units of k for an nth-order reaction: mol^{1−n}·L^{n−1}·s⁻¹.
t½: zero order [A]₀/2k; first order 0.693/k; second order 1/(k[A]₀).
A first-order plot of ln[A] vs t is a straight line of slope −k.
After n half-lives of a first-order reaction, (1/2)ⁿ of the reactant remains.
Arrhenius: k = Ae^{−Ea/RT}; ln(k₂/k₁) = (Ea/R)(1/T₁ − 1/T₂).
A catalyst lowers Ea through an alternative path; it changes neither ΔH nor K.
The slow (rate-determining) step fixes the rate law of a mechanism.
Pseudo-first-order: an excess reactant makes a higher-order reaction behave as first-order.
Oxidation-number rules: F always −1; O usually −2 (peroxides −1, OF₂ +2); H is +1 with nonmetals, −1 in hydrides.
Disproportionation: one species is both oxidised and reduced (Cl₂ + 2OH⁻ → Cl⁻ + ClO⁻ + H₂O).
n-factor: KMnO₄/H⁺ = 5, K₂Cr₂O₇/H⁺ = 6, H₂SO₄ (dibasic) = 2.
Close-packed lattice: 1 octahedral + 2 tetrahedral voids per atom.
Radius-ratio limits: tetrahedral 0.225–0.414, octahedral 0.414–0.732, cubic 0.732–1.0.
Packing efficiency: simple cubic 52%, BCC 68%, FCC/HCP 74%.
Schottky defect lowers density; Frenkel defect leaves density unchanged.
Chelate effect: polydentate ligands give extra-stable complexes — largely entropy-driven.

oneliners.text: NVIDIA's RTX Spark laptops launch on 16 October 2026 with an updated software ecosystem for AI agents and creative tools.

oneliners.subject: Technology
oneliners.text: NVIDIA PAIR (Personal AI Router) moved out of beta on 13 Oct 2026 — free, open source, with llama.cpp support and Hugging Face downloads.

oneliners.subject: Physics
oneliners.text: DRDO’s Astra programme roadmap: Astra Mk-1 (~100 km, in IAF service), Astra Mk-2 (>200 km), and Project Gandiva / Astra Mk-3 (>300 km).

oneliners.subject: Exam Updates
oneliners.text: JEE Main 2027 eligibility (expected): Class 12 passed in 2025/2026 or appearing in 2027; for NITs/IIITs - 75% in Class 12 or top-20 percentile of the board (65% for SC/ST) (Oct 2026).

oneliners.subject: Exam Updates
oneliners.text: JEE Main 2027 fees (expected): Rs 1,000 (Gen male), Rs 800 (Gen female), Rs 900/Rs 800 (Gen-EWS/OBC male/female), Rs 500 (SC/ST/PwD/Transgender) (Oct 2026).

oneliners.subject: Exam Updates
oneliners.text: JEE Main 2027 application (expected): 3 steps - registration via Aadhaar/DigiLocker, form fill-up with photo, signature and Class-X certificate, then online fee payment (Oct 2026).

oneliners.subject: Practice Paper
oneliners.text: NEET UG 2027 will be conducted in CBT mode; the final decision on the shift awaits the report of the Nandan Nilekani-led task force.

oneliners.subject: Practice Paper
oneliners.text: GATE 2027 registration reopened with a late fee; the extended last date is 16 Oct 2026 (reported 15 Oct 2026).

oneliners.subject: NTA updates
oneliners.text: JEE Main 2027 Session 1 application is expected to close in the fourth week of November 2026.

oneliners.subject: NTA updates
oneliners.text: All NTA 2026-27 calendar dates are tentative; the official information bulletin will be published separately for each exam.

oneliners.subject: Physics
oneliners.text: JEE Main 2027 Session 1 is tentatively set for 22–24 and 28–30 January 2027 (buffer 31 January); registration expected late October–November 2026 at jeemain.nta.nic.in.

oneliners.subject: Chemistry
oneliners.text: JEE Main Paper 1: 75 questions, 300 marks, 3 hours, with −1 for every wrong answer including numerical-value questions.

oneliners.subject: Maths
oneliners.text: JEE Main has no age limit; Class 12 passed in 2025 or 2026, or appearing in 2027, is the expected eligibility for the 2027 cycle.

oneliners.subject: Current Affairs
oneliners.text: NTA is expected to open JEE Main 2027 Session 1 registration in the last week of October or early November 2026 at jeemain.nta.nic.in (tentative exam: 22-30 January 2027).

oneliners.subject: Current Affairs
oneliners.text: JEE Main 2027 Session 2 registration is expected in February 2027 with the exam likely in April 2027.

oneliners.subject: Current Affairs
oneliners.text: JEE Main 2027 eligibility: Class 12 passed in 2025 or 2026, or appearing in 2027; 75% marks (65% for SC/ST) needed for NIT/IIIT/CFTI admission; top 2,50,000 Paper-1 candidates qualify for JEE Advanced (2026 general cut-off: 93.41 percentile).

oneliners.subject: Current Affairs
oneliners.text: JEE Main 2027 Session 1: 22, 23, 24, 28, 29 and 30 January 2027 (31 January is the buffer day); registration expected in late October 2026 on jeemain.nta.nic.in; the paper is offered in 13 languages, with the English version prevailing on any discrepancy.

oneliners.subject: Current Affairs
oneliners.text: IIT Delhi will conduct JEE (Advanced) 2027; the NTA notes that all its 2027 examination dates are tentative and may change for administrative or logistical reasons.

oneliners.subject: Exam Updates
oneliners.text: A parliamentary panel has recommended at least one permanent computer-based test centre in every district for NTA exams including JEE Main; last year 16.04 lakh registered for JEE Main and 15.38 lakh appeared. (21 Oct 2026)

oneliners.subject: Exam Updates
oneliners.text: The panel's 35 recommendations include an independent mechanism to audit examination security, investigate candidates' grievances and report directly to the Education Ministry, plus compensation for candidates affected by administrative cancellations. (21 Oct 2026)

oneliners.subject: Physics
oneliners.text: 21 Oct 2026: The 12th World Green Economy Summit (Dubai) notes solar PV and lithium-battery costs have fallen ~90% since 2010 — the learning-curve economics behind energy-transition problems.

oneliners.text: 22 Oct 2026: JEE Main 2027 Session 1 on 22, 23, 24, 28, 29 & 30 January 2027 (buffer 31 Jan); registration expected late Oct 2026 at jeemain.nta.nic.in.

oneliners.text: 23 Oct 2026: JEE Main 2026 was conducted by NTA in two sessions (January and April); JEE Advanced 2026 followed in May 2026.

alerts.title: JEE Main Session 1 registration expected 28 Oct – 1 Nov (not yet open)
alerts.body: Registration has not opened yet. Based on NTA's pattern of recent years it is expected between 28 October and 1 November, for the exam on 22–30 January (31 January buffer). Watch only jeemain.nta.nic.in — ignore “registration open” claims on unofficial sites.
